Accountable obligation owner.value: Controller owns the statutory close and the signed NAIC Annual/Quarterly Statement blank for every writing company; the Statutory Reporting Manager runs the preparation cycle day to day

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 7 Standard 7.11 (reliable, transparent financial reporting subject to independent external audit) read against the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions and the domiciliary state's permitted/prescribed practice list; re-verified each December when the NAIC Blanks (E) Working Group publishes the year's blank and instruction changes

In-scope processes.value: Statutory close for each writing company: GL trial balance → SSAP adjustments and nonadmitted assets → Pages 2-5 (Assets, Liabilities/Surplus, Summary of Operations, Cash Flow) → Exhibits 1-8, Analysis of Operations, Notes and General Interrogatories → officer jurat

In-scope systems.value: NAIC blanks software fed by the ERP general ledger trial balance, with reserve, investment and reinsurance feeds; cross-check edits cleared inside the blanks software before the period is locked

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statutory Financial Statement Preparation Procedure — close calendar, GL-to-blank account mapping, SSAP adjustment schedule, exhibit ownership matrix, cross-check clearance rules, jurat signing and lock

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and re-approved annually once the year's NAIC blank changes are adopted; interim changes to the GL-to-blank mapping need Controller approval on the change log

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual Statement blank complete and jurat-signed by March 1; quarterly statements by the 45th day after quarter end (May 15, August 15, November 15); internal lock 10 business days before each date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Close-calendar tasks per writing company with alerts at T-20, T-10 and T-3 business days to the internal lock, escalating to the Controller on any task still open at T-3

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Locked blank PDF, jurat, trial-balance-to-blank tie-out, SSAP adjustment support, exhibit reconciliations and the cross-check clearance report retained 7 years in the financial reporting repository under <company>-<statement period>

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Cross-check edits waived at lock, post-lock reclassifications, and any amended statement are logged with cause, the affected blank line and the disposition approved by the Controller

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs the jurat and personally approves every amended blank or restated line before it leaves the company

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every Annual and Quarterly Statement blank prepared in the period for each writing company, together with the closed GL trial balances, reserve summaries and holdings files that fed them

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero dollar variance between Pages 2-4 and the closed trial balance; zero unresolved NAIC cross-check edits at lock; any statement not jurat-signed by March 1 or the 45th day is a fail and goes straight to the CFO

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly and annual; full tie-out and exhibit re-performance on the annual blank, targeted tie-out of Pages 2-4 and the reserve/investment exhibits on each quarterly

Evidence location for test results.value: Statutory statement preparation test workpaper (population, tie-out, exhibit re-performance, cross-check log, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under <company>-<statement period>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Locked blank, jurat, GL tie-out, SSAP adjustment schedule and cross-check clearance report producible for a domiciliary financial examination or an NAIC Financial Analysis Division inquiry within 5 business days

checklist.step: Open the statutory filing period for every writing company
actions: In the statutory blanks software create the filing period for each writing company, entering NAIC company code, group code, FEIN and state of domicile from the company demographic record.
Load the current-year blank version and Annual Statement Instructions, and confirm with the Controller which blank each entity files — Life/Fraternal, Property, Health or Title.
Cross-check the entity list against the Certificates of Authority held so no licensed writing company is missing a filing period.

Publish the close calendar to Accounting, Actuarial, Investments, Reinsurance and Tax with the internal lock date set 10 business days before March 1 (annual) or the 45th day after quarter end (quarterly).
Record the blank version number and instruction release date on the cycle cover sheet in the financial reporting repository.
checklist.done: every writing company has an open period on the current-year blank and a published close calendar with a dated lock.

checklist.step: Import the closed trial balance and clear the blank mapping
actions: Wait for the close sign-off in the close/consolidation tool, then run the period-end trial balance by company and legal entity in the ERP general ledger.

Import the trial balance into the blanks software and run the mapping report so every account resolves to a Page 2 (Assets), Page 3 (Liabilities, Surplus and Other Funds) or Page 4 (Summary of Operations) line.
Work the unmapped-account exception list to zero with the Controller — accounts opened during the year are the usual cause — and record each new mapping on the mapping change log.
Print the trial-balance-to-blank tie-out showing total assets, total liabilities and total capital and surplus agreeing to the GL to the dollar, and file it in the statement evidence folder.
checklist.done: the trial balance imports with zero unmapped accounts and Pages 2-4 agree to the closed GL to the dollar.

checklist.step: Book the statutory-only adjustments and the nonadmitted asset schedule
actions: Build the nonadmitted asset schedule: agents' balances over 90 days past due, EDP equipment and software above the SSAP 16 admissibility limit, furniture and fixtures, prepaid expenses, and deferred tax assets failing the SSAP 101 admissibility test.
Post each statutory-only entry as its own journal in the statutory ledger with a memo naming the SSAP that requires it, so the GAAP-to-SAP bridge is readable line by line.
Recompute the change in nonadmitted assets versus the prior year-end and confirm it lands on the 'Change in nonadmitted assets' line of the Capital and Surplus Account on Page 4.
Have a Senior Accountant who did not prepare the schedule re-add it, initial and date the review, and file it with the tie-out.
checklist.done: every statutory-only entry cites its SSAP and the change in nonadmitted assets flows correctly to the Capital and Surplus Account.

checklist.step: Load invested assets and build the investment schedules and exhibits
actions: Export the statement-date holdings file with CUSIP/ISIN, NAIC designation, book/adjusted carrying value, fair value, acquisition date and par for every position.

Confirm each bond carries a current NAIC designation from the Securities Valuation Office or a filing-exempt CRP rating; hand unrated or newly acquired private placements to the Investment Analyst for SVO filing before the lock.
Build Schedule D Parts 1-6, Schedule DA (short-term), Schedule DB Parts A-D (derivatives, per ICP 15 Standard 15.7) and Schedule E (cash, deposits and short-term investments) in the blanks software.
Prepare the Exhibit of Net Investment Income and the Exhibit of Capital Gains (Losses) and reconcile both to the GL investment income and realised gain accounts.
Tie Schedule D Part 1 and Part 2 totals to the bonds and stocks lines on Page 2 and file the reconciliation.
checklist.done: Schedules D, DA, DB and E tie to Page 2, every holding carries a current NAIC designation, and investment income ties to the GL.

checklist.step: Load actuarial reserves and build the reserve exhibits
actions: Take the signed reserve summary from the production valuation run and record the valuation date, reserve basis (CRVM/VM-20 or loss reserve basis) and the model version and run identifier.

Load aggregate reserves for life contracts (Exhibit 5), accident and health reserves (Exhibit 6) and liabilities for deposit-type contracts (Exhibit 7) — or, on a property blank, Schedule P Parts 1-4 and the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit.
Reconcile the reserve rollforward (opening balance, new business, releases, interest accretion, closing balance) to the Page 3 reserve lines and to the Analysis of Operations by line of business.
Obtain the Appointed Actuary's written confirmation that the loaded figures are the exact amounts the Statement of Actuarial Opinion filed with the blank will cover.
File the reserve summary, rollforward and confirmation in the statement evidence folder.
checklist.done: the reserve exhibits tie to Page 3 and the Appointed Actuary has confirmed the loaded amounts in writing.

checklist.step: Load ceded and assumed reinsurance and compute the provision for reinsurance
actions: Extract ceded and assumed premium, ceded reserves, paid and unpaid recoverables and funds held, keyed on each counterparty's NAIC company code, AM Best ID or FEIN.
Confirm each reinsurer's status at the statement date — authorized, certified, reciprocal jurisdiction or unauthorized — from the domiciliary state list and the NAIC certified reinsurer listing.
Compute the provision for reinsurance on unauthorized balances lacking qualifying collateral and post it to the Page 3 provision line.
Build Schedule F (property) or Schedule S (life) parts and tie ceded balances to the recoverable line on Page 2 and the ceded premium on Exhibit 1.
Reconcile letters of credit and trust balances to the treaty repository and flag to the Reinsurance Manager any LOC expiring within 90 days of the statement date.
checklist.done: Schedule F/S ties to the balance sheet and every unauthorized balance has qualifying collateral or a booked provision.

checklist.step: Build the premium and state allocation exhibits
actions: Extract direct written premium, direct earned premium, direct losses paid and direct losses unpaid by state and by annual statement line of business for the statement period.

Build Schedule T (Exhibit of Premiums Written allocated by state and territory) and confirm the state grand total agrees to direct written premium on Exhibit 1 / the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit.
Reconcile the state split to the premium tax working papers held by the Tax Manager and clear every difference before the lock rather than after.
Run the licence cross-check: any state/line combination carrying premium where the entity holds no Certificate of Authority is escalated to the Producer Compliance Manager the same day.
checklist.done: Schedule T agrees to Exhibit 1 and to the premium tax working papers, with no premium allocated to an unlicensed state/line.

checklist.step: Assemble the statement pages and the Analysis of Operations
actions: Generate Pages 2 through 5 and confirm Page 5 (Cash Flow) reconciles to the movement in Schedule E cash and short-term investments.
Build the Analysis of Operations by Lines of Business and confirm the total column agrees to the Summary of Operations on Page 4.
Complete Exhibit 1 (Premiums and Annuity Considerations), Exhibit 2 (General Expenses), Exhibit 3 (Taxes, Licenses and Fees) and Exhibit 8 (Miscellaneous), tying each to its GL source.
Collect the exhibit owner sign-offs — Investments, Actuarial, Reinsurance, Tax — onto the exhibit ownership matrix before assembly is called complete.
checklist.done: all statement pages, the Analysis of Operations and Exhibits 1-8 are assembled, internally consistent and signed by their exhibit owners.

checklist.step: Draft the Notes to Financial Statements and the General Interrogatories
actions: Roll forward each of the NAIC-numbered Notes to Financial Statements and refresh the numbers from this period's ledger — do not carry a prior-year figure into a current-year note.

Draft Note 1 (summary of significant accounting policies), Note 2 (accounting changes and corrections of errors) and the permitted/prescribed practice disclosure, quoting the domiciliary state's approval letter where one exists.
Answer the General Interrogatories Parts 1 and 2 with the source for each answer — holding company registration, custodial agreements, officer/director conflicts and the fidelity bond amount.
Route every note and interrogatory answer involving legal or governance facts to the Corporate Secretary for confirmation.
File the answered interrogatory support pack with the statement evidence.
checklist.done: every note and interrogatory answer is refreshed from current-period data and sourced, with legal/governance answers confirmed by the Corporate Secretary.

checklist.step: Run the NAIC cross-checks and clear every edit
actions: Run the full cross-check/validation routine in the blanks software and export the edit report.
Work each edit to a resolution: correct the underlying figure where the edit is right, or record the explanation the NAIC instructions permit where a legitimate difference exists.
Re-run the routine after every correction and keep the final clean edit report — never lock on a stale run.
List any edit answered by explanation rather than correction on the exception log for Controller approval.
checklist.done: the final edit report shows no unresolved cross-checks and every explained edit has Controller approval on the exception log.

checklist.step: Reconcile the surplus rollforward and agree the prior filing
actions: Roll capital and surplus from the prior filed statement to this one: net income, change in net unrealised gains, change in nonadmitted assets, change in provision for reinsurance, change in deferred tax, dividends and capital contributions.
Agree the opening balance line by line to the prior filed blank as filed, not to the internal ledger, and explain any difference as a correction of error under SSAP 3.
Confirm each rollforward component ties to its supporting exhibit, and where a component moves more than 10% of surplus, attach a written driver explanation.
Sign and date the surplus rollforward as the Controller's own review evidence.
checklist.done: surplus rolls from the prior filed blank to this one with every component tied to an exhibit and large movements explained.

checklist.step: Tie the blank to the risk-based capital calculation
actions: Feed the locked draft blank into the RBC formula and confirm each RBC input page pulls its figures from the matching blank page, schedule or exhibit.
Recompute Total Adjusted Capital and Authorized Control Level RBC and compare the resulting ratio to the prior year and to the company's board-approved capital target.
Where the ratio falls into or near an action level, notify the Chief Financial Officer and the Chief Risk Officer in writing before the statement is signed.
File the RBC-to-blank reconciliation alongside the statement evidence.
checklist.done: RBC inputs reconcile to the blank and the resulting ratio, with any action-level proximity, is reported to the CFO in writing.

checklist.step: Run the officer review pack and sign the jurat
actions: Review the officer pack: Pages 2-5, the surplus rollforward, the exception log, the clean edit report, the RBC reconciliation and the Appointed Actuary's confirmation.
Confirm the jurat page carries the correct company name, NAIC code, statutory home office and mailing address, and the names and titles of the officers and directors required to attest.
Sign the jurat with the CFO and the second required officer, dated on or before the internal lock date, and have it notarised where the domiciliary state requires it.
Return any page carrying an open question to the Statutory Reporting Manager rather than signing subject to a follow-up.
checklist.done: the jurat is signed and dated by the required officers with no open questions on any statement page.

checklist.step: Lock the blank and hand the filing set to Regulatory Reporting
actions: Lock the filing period in the blanks software so no figure can move after the jurat date, and generate the NAIC-format export file plus the print PDF.
Assemble the filing set: export file, print PDF, signed jurat, Statement of Actuarial Opinion and the state-specific attachments named on the domiciliary checklist.
Hand the set to the Regulatory Reporting Manager with the filing deadline stated on the transmittal, and log the handover date and time.
Keep the blanks software period locked; any later change must be raised as an amended statement, never as an edit to the locked period.
checklist.done: the period is locked and a complete filing set is handed to Regulatory Reporting with a logged handover ahead of the deadline.

checklist.step: Archive the statement evidence file
actions: Move the full evidence folder — trial-balance tie-out, SSAP adjustment schedule, exhibit reconciliations, edit report, surplus rollforward, RBC reconciliation, notes support and signed jurat — into the financial reporting repository under <company>-<statement period>.
Apply the 7-year retention label and restrict edit rights to the Controller so the filed record cannot be altered after the fact.
Confirm the repository index makes the record searchable by NAIC company code, statement period and blank type for examiner requests.
Record the archive completion on the close calendar as the cycle's closing task.
checklist.done: the complete statement evidence file is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by NAIC code and statement period.

testing.step: Build the population of statements prepared in the period
actions: List every filing period locked in the blanks software during the test period, by writing company, blank type and statement period.
Reconcile the list to the entity register and the Certificates of Authority held so no licensed writing company is missing a statement.
Pull for each population row the closed trial balance, the reserve summary, the holdings file and the signed jurat, and note any missing input before sampling.
Have the extractor sign the population as complete and date it.
testing.done: the statement population is reconciled to the entity register with every supporting input identified and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the filed pages back to the closed general ledger
actions: Re-run the period-end trial balance in the ERP for each population entity, independent of the copy the preparer used.
Agree total assets, total liabilities and total capital and surplus on Pages 2 and 3 of the locked blank to that trial balance plus the statutory-only journals.
List every statutory-only journal not carrying an SSAP reference in its memo as an exception.
Record any dollar variance, however small, with its explanation — an unexplained variance is a fail, not a rounding note.
testing.done: each statement's Pages 2-3 reconcile to an independently extracted trial balance with every adjustment SSAP-referenced.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of statement lines and exhibits
actions: Take 100% of the reserve lines, the Schedule F/S provision for reinsurance and the nonadmitted asset schedule for every entity.
Select 20 further balance-sheet and operations lines at random using a recorded seed, weighted to the largest dollar movements versus the prior filing.
Record the seed, the population size, the selection date and the entity coverage in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
Confirm the sample touches at least one quarterly statement per entity as well as the annual.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is drawn covering all reserve, reinsurance-provision and nonadmitted lines plus 20 seeded random lines.

testing.step: Re-perform the nonadmitted asset and SSAP admissibility judgement
actions: Take the agents' balances ageing straight from the billing system and recompute the amount over 90 days past due at the statement date.
Re-apply the SSAP 16 limit to EDP equipment and operating software and the SSAP 101 paragraph 11 admissibility test to deferred tax assets without reading the preparer's schedule first.
Compare your figure to the booked nonadmitted amount; any difference above the workpaper's dollar tolerance is an exception including 'right amount, wrong SSAP basis'.
Capture the ageing report and the deferred tax admissibility computation into the workpaper.
testing.done: each nonadmitted category is independently recomputed and agreed, or the difference is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Trace sampled investment holdings to Schedule D and to a current NAIC designation
actions: Select 25 holdings from the statement-date custody position file and trace each by CUSIP to its Schedule D Part 1 or Part 2 line.
Confirm the book/adjusted carrying value on the schedule agrees to the investment accounting record and the fair value source is named.
Verify the NAIC designation shown is supported by a current SVO assignment or an eligible filing-exempt CRP rating at the statement date, not a prior-year designation.
Agree Schedule D totals to the Page 2 bonds and stocks lines and capture the reconciliation.
testing.done: every sampled holding traces to Schedule D at the right value with a designation valid at the statement date.

testing.step: Re-perform the reinsurance provision and the Schedule F/S counterparty status
actions: Take the ten largest ceded recoverable balances and confirm each counterparty's authorized/certified/reciprocal status at the statement date from the domiciliary state list, not from the prior year's file.
Recompute the provision for reinsurance on unauthorized balances net of qualifying collateral and compare to the booked Page 3 provision.
Trace each claimed letter of credit or trust to the instrument in the treaty repository and confirm it was in force and unexpired at the statement date.
Log any collateral that expired before the statement date as an exception with the surplus impact quantified.
testing.done: the reinsurance provision recomputes to the booked amount with every counterparty status and collateral instrument verified at the statement date.

testing.step: Verify Schedule T against the premium source and the licensing register
actions: Independently extract direct written premium by state and annual statement line for the statement period and compare it to Schedule T state by state.
Agree the Schedule T grand total to Exhibit 1 direct written premium and to the premium tax working papers.
Cross-check each state/line carrying premium against the Certificate of Authority register and list any unlicensed state/line as a reportable breach, not a test exception.
Capture the state-level comparison into the workpaper.
testing.done: Schedule T agrees to an independent premium extract and to Exhibit 1, with every state/line covered by a Certificate of Authority.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline maths and check the cross-check clearance
actions: Recompute each statement's due date — March 1 for the annual, the 45th day after quarter end for each quarterly — and compare it to the jurat signature date and the lock date.
Confirm the internal lock date preceded the due date by the 10 business days the procedure requires and list any cycle that ran into the buffer.
Open the final cross-check edit report retained for each sampled statement and confirm it is the run that followed the last correction, with no unresolved edits.
Test every edit closed by explanation for a documented Controller approval on the exception log.
testing.done: every statement was jurat-signed before its statutory date and locked on a clean, final edit report with approved explanations.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the entity, statement period, blank line or schedule, the dollar effect and whether surplus was misstated.
Assign a root cause — unmapped GL account, stale NAIC designation, expired collateral, late actuarial feed, missed cross-check — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date inside the next statement cycle and, where surplus was misstated, open an amended-statement assessment with the Controller and CFO.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a quantified surplus effect, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the statement preparation test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-variance and zero-unresolved-edit thresholds and summarise the surplus effect of all exceptions combined.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each statement.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared no page or exhibit in the tested statements, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any surplus misstatement to the Audit Committee at its next meeting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with an exception rate, a quantified surplus effect, a stated conclusion and an Audit Committee reporting date.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual Statement and RBC filed by March 1; quarterlies by May 15, August 15 and November 15; state-specific earlier or hard-copy dates tracked individually on the per-state matrix

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing tracker alerts at T-10, T-5 and T-1 business days per state per filing, with a same-day escalation to the Controller if no confirmation receipt is logged by the due date

checklist.step: Rebuild the state/filing matrix for the cycle
actions: Pull the current Certificate of Authority list per writing company and expand it into one matrix row per state per filing (annual blank, each quarterly, RBC, actuarial opinion, supplements).

For each row read the state's entry in the NAIC Annual Financial Reporting Checklist and record: required or waived, electronic or hard copy, whether an original signed jurat is demanded, the filing fee and the payment method.
Check each state DOI bulletin page for filing changes issued since the last cycle and update the row, noting the bulletin number and date.
Publish the matrix to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and lock it as the cycle's control document.
checklist.done: the matrix carries one sourced row per state per filing with channel, format, fee and jurat requirement recorded.

checklist.step: Accept the locked filing set from Statutory Reporting
actions: Receive the handover transmittal and confirm the period is locked in the blanks software so no figure can shift after transmission.
Check the set is complete: NAIC-format export file, print PDF, signed jurat, Statement of Actuarial Opinion and any state-specific attachment named on the matrix.
Open the print PDF and confirm the company name, NAIC company code, statement period and blank type on the jurat match the matrix rows.
Reject the set back to the Statutory Reporting Manager if any element is missing rather than filing a partial set.
checklist.done: a complete, locked filing set is accepted with the jurat identifiers agreeing to the matrix.

checklist.step: Validate the export file against the NAIC filing specification
actions: Run the NAIC filing validation on the export file and clear every structural and cross-check error before any upload attempt.
Confirm the file header carries the correct NAIC company code, group code, statement year, quarter and blank type — a wrong header is the most common rejection.
Check the file size and format against the current NAIC filing specification and confirm the software's filing version matches the NAIC-published version for the year.
Save the clean validation report with the export file as pre-submission evidence.
checklist.done: the export file passes NAIC validation cleanly with a correct header and a saved validation report.

checklist.step: Upload the filing to the NAIC Financial Data Repository
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ with the company's filing credentials and open the Financial Data Repository filing upload for the statement period.
Upload the export file and the PDF, select the correct statement type and period, and submit.
Wait for the repository's acceptance response rather than assuming success; if the upload is rejected, read the error, fix the underlying file and resubmit the same day.
Download the acceptance confirmation showing filing date, time, company code and statement type, and file it in the compliance evidence repository.
Record the confirmation reference on every matrix row the upload satisfies.
checklist.done: the NAIC upload is accepted and the dated confirmation is filed and referenced on the matrix.

checklist.step: File with the domiciliary state on its own terms
actions: Read the domiciliary state's filing instructions in full — domiciliary states routinely demand more than the NAIC upload, including originals and state-only supplements.
Submit through the state's own portal or email address where the matrix says the NAIC upload does not satisfy the state.
Where an original signed jurat is required, courier it with tracking to the DOI address on the matrix and retain the proof of delivery.
Pay the domiciliary filing fee by the method the state accepts and file the payment confirmation with the receipt.
checklist.done: the domiciliary state has its full filing set, its original jurat where required, and its fee, all with dated proof.

checklist.step: File with every non-domiciliary state of licensure
actions: Work the matrix state by state, filing only what each state actually requires — many states accept the NAIC repository filing and require nothing further, and over-filing hides genuine gaps.
For states requiring a direct submission, upload through the named state portal and capture the on-screen confirmation number.
For states requiring hard copy, print the blank, attach the signed jurat and courier it with tracking to the address on the matrix.
Mark each matrix row filed only when a confirmation reference, portal receipt or courier delivery record exists — never on the strength of a sent email.
Escalate to the Regulatory Reporting Manager any state whose portal is unavailable within 3 business days of the due date.
checklist.done: every non-domiciliary matrix row is either marked not-required with its source or filed with a captured confirmation reference.

checklist.step: Pay filing fees and reconcile them to the finance ledger
actions: Build the fee schedule from the matrix — amount, state, payment method (EFT, state portal card payment, cheque) and due date.
Raise the payments in the ERP and confirm each clears before the filing due date, since several states treat an unpaid fee as an unfiled statement.
Reconcile the cleared payments back to the matrix rows and to the Exhibit of Taxes, Licenses and Fees, and chase any unmatched item.
File the payment confirmations alongside the filing receipts.
checklist.done: every fee on the matrix is paid, cleared before the due date and reconciled to the ledger and the filing receipts.

checklist.step: File the RBC report where the state requires it separately
actions: Generate the RBC filing from the locked blank and confirm Total Adjusted Capital and Authorized Control Level RBC agree to the reconciliation signed at close.
Upload the RBC filing to the NAIC repository with the March 1 annual statement submission.
File the RBC report separately with the domiciliary state and with each state whose matrix row demands a direct RBC filing.
Where the ratio sits at or below a company action level, notify Regulatory Counsel and the CFO before filing so the accompanying plan requirement is understood.
checklist.done: the RBC filing is submitted to the NAIC and to every state requiring it, with any action-level trigger notified before submission.

checklist.step: File the Statement of Actuarial Opinion and its supporting documents
actions: Confirm the signed Statement of Actuarial Opinion names the same reserve amounts loaded into the filed blank and carries the actuary's qualification statement.
File the opinion with the annual statement to the NAIC repository and to each state whose matrix row requires it directly.
Prepare the supporting actuarial memorandum and the regulatory asset adequacy issues summary and hold them ready for the domiciliary commissioner on request or by the state's stated date.

Record the opinion type — unqualified, qualified, adverse or inconclusive — on the matrix, and where it is anything but unqualified notify the Chief Financial Officer and Regulatory Counsel the same day.
checklist.done: the actuarial opinion is filed with the statement, its type is recorded, and the supporting memorandum is ready for the domiciliary regulator.

checklist.step: Capture and index every confirmation receipt
actions: For each filed matrix row save the confirmation artifact — repository acceptance, portal receipt number screenshot, courier proof of delivery or state acknowledgement email.
Name each file <company>-<state>-<filing>-<yyyy-mm-dd> and index it by NAIC company code, state and filing type.
Enter the confirmation reference and the confirmed filing date onto the matrix row so the matrix, not a folder, is the completeness record.
Flag any row still without a confirmation 2 business days after submission and chase the state directly.
checklist.done: every filed row carries an indexed confirmation artifact and a confirmed filing date on the matrix.

checklist.step: Close the completeness review before the due date
actions: Two business days before each due date, run the matrix for rows with no confirmation reference and treat each as an open filing.
Assign each open row to a named analyst with a same-day completion instruction and confirm closure personally.
Where a state cannot be filed by the due date, request a written extension from that DOI before the deadline, never after, and record the request and response on the row.
Report the completeness position to the Controller on the due date.
checklist.done: on each due date every matrix row is confirmed filed, formally extended, or reported to the Controller as late.

checklist.step: Handle rejections and state objections
actions: Log every rejected upload or state objection notice on the tracker within 1 business day, with the state, the stated reason and the original filing date.
Diagnose whether the cause is a file/header defect, a missing attachment, an unpaid fee or a substantive figure, and route figure issues back to the Statutory Reporting Manager.
Resubmit the corrected filing and capture the fresh confirmation, keeping both the rejection notice and the successful receipt on the record.
Note on the tracker whether the state treats the resubmission date or the original date as the filing date, because that determines lateness.
checklist.done: every rejection is logged, diagnosed, resubmitted with a fresh confirmation, and its effective filing date established.

checklist.step: Control amended filings
actions: Assess any post-filing error against the domiciliary state's amendment threshold and the surplus effect before deciding to amend.
Where an amendment is required, have the blanks software period reopened under change control, correct only the affected lines, and re-lock and re-jurat the statement.
Notify the domiciliary DOI in writing of the amendment and its cause before uploading the amended filing.
Re-file the amended statement to the NAIC repository and to every state that received the original, and capture new confirmations for each.
checklist.done: each amendment is approved, notified to the domiciliary regulator, re-jurated and re-filed everywhere the original went, with new confirmations.

checklist.step: Report filing timeliness to management
actions: Publish per cycle the timeliness metrics: rows due, rows filed on time, rows filed late with day counts, extensions granted and rejections.
Attach the root cause of every late row and the owner of its corrective action.
Table the metrics at the Compliance Committee and record any regulator penalty or late-filing notice received.
Feed repeat-offender states into the next cycle's matrix as early-start rows.
checklist.done: the cycle's timeliness metrics, causes and owners are reported to the Compliance Committee and carried into the next cycle.

checklist.step: Archive the cycle's filing evidence
actions: Archive the completed matrix, every confirmation artifact, the fee reconciliation, extension correspondence and rejection/resubmission records as one cycle folder.
Apply the 7-year retention label and make the folder read-only outside the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Confirm the folder is searchable by NAIC company code, state, filing type and filing date for examiner requests.
Close the cycle on the filing calendar.
checklist.done: the cycle folder is archived, retention-labelled, read-only and searchable by state and filing type.

testing.step: Rebuild the population of filings that were due in the cycle
actions: Independently expand the current Certificate of Authority register into one required row per writing company per state per filing type, without using the preparer's matrix.
Compare your expansion to the cycle matrix and investigate every row present in one and not the other.
Confirm states added or surrendered during the year are picked up from the effective dates on the CoA register.
Sign the reconciled population as complete and date it.
testing.done: an independently built population reconciles to the cycle matrix with every difference investigated.

testing.step: Verify each required row against the NAIC state filing checklist
actions: For 20 sampled states read the current NAIC Annual Financial Reporting Checklist entry and reach your own view on what that state requires and in what format.
Compare your view to the matrix row's channel, format, jurat and fee fields; a wrong channel field is an exception even where the filing arrived.
Check the matrix cites a bulletin or checklist date for any row marked not-required, and treat an unsourced 'not required' as a fail.
Screenshot the checklist entries relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled state's requirement is independently confirmed and every not-required row carries a verifiable source.

testing.step: Draw the sample of filings for receipt testing
actions: Take 100% of domiciliary-state rows, all hard-copy rows and all RBC and actuarial opinion rows.
Select 30 further rows at random using a recorded seed across the remaining states and quarterly filings.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and coverage so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every row that suffered a rejection during the cycle to the sample as a mandatory item.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is drawn covering domiciliary, hard-copy, RBC, opinion and previously rejected rows.

testing.step: Trace sampled filings to a genuine regulator confirmation
actions: Open the confirmation artifact for each sampled row and confirm it names the company, NAIC code, state, statement period and filing type.
Reject a sent-mail record, an internal note or an unnumbered screenshot as evidence — only a regulator-issued acceptance, portal receipt number or courier delivery record counts.
For NAIC repository rows, re-open iSite+ and confirm the filing appears against the company code and period with the same date shown on the artifact.
List any row whose artifact cannot be corroborated in the regulator's own system.
testing.done: every sampled row is corroborated by a regulator-issued confirmation matching the artifact on file.

testing.step: Recompute the due-date and lateness maths
actions: Recompute each sampled row's due date — March 1 for annual and RBC, the 45th day after quarter end for quarterlies, or the state-specific date on the matrix.
Compare the confirmed filing date to the due date and compute days late where applicable, treating the state's own effective-filing-date convention for resubmissions.
For any row claiming an extension, read the DOI's written grant and confirm it was requested before the original due date.
Tabulate every late row with its day count and the state involved.
testing.done: every sampled row has a recomputed due date, a measured lateness and, where claimed, a verified pre-deadline extension.

testing.step: Test that the filed figures match the locked statement
actions: For 10 sampled rows download the filing as it sits in the NAIC repository and compare Pages 2, 3 and 4 to the locked blank retained internally.
Confirm the jurat date on the filed copy equals the internally signed jurat date and the signing officers are the same.
Any figure difference between the filed and retained copies is a reportable exception, since it means an unlocked file was transmitted.
Capture the comparison into the workpaper.
testing.done: the filed copies match the locked internal statements page for page with identical jurat dates and signatories.

testing.step: Verify filing fees were paid and cleared before the due dates
actions: Trace each sampled row's fee from the matrix to a cleared payment in the ERP with the state as payee.
Compare the payment clearing date to the filing due date and flag any fee cleared after it.
Reconcile total fees paid for the cycle to the Exhibit of Taxes, Licenses and Fees and explain the difference.
List unpaid or short-paid fees as exceptions with the state's treatment of an unpaid fee noted.
testing.done: every sampled fee traces to a cleared, timely payment and total fees reconcile to the taxes, licenses and fees exhibit.

testing.step: Re-perform the rejection and amendment handling
actions: Pull every rejection and amendment logged in the cycle and confirm each was logged within 1 business day of the notice.
Confirm each amendment carries Controller approval, a re-locked and re-jurated statement, written notice to the domiciliary DOI and a fresh confirmation from every state that received the original.
Check no amended figure was pushed to one state and not another, which leaves inconsistent statements on the public record.
List any amendment filed without prior domiciliary notice as an exception.
testing.done: every rejection and amendment is logged, approved, re-jurated and re-filed consistently across all recipients.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the company, state, filing type, days late and whether a regulator notice or penalty followed.
Assign a root cause — stale matrix, missed CoA change, portal outage, unpaid fee, header defect, late handover from Statutory Reporting — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date inside the current cycle where the filing is still open, and inside the next cycle for process fixes.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the filing timeliness test
actions: Compute on-time completeness as confirmed-on-time rows divided by required rows and compare it to the 100% threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper reference behind each late or missing row.
Have the independent reviewer, who transmitted no filing in the cycle, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, the late list and any DOI penalty notice to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with an on-time completeness rate, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Controller owns the annual supplemental schedule and exhibit pack; each supplement has a named preparer on the supplement ownership matrix (Investments, Actuarial, Reinsurance, HR Compensation, Tax)

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 15 Standards 15.6-15.8 (investment and derivatives reporting, per the ICP 15.7 derivatives standard behind Schedule DB) and ICP 22 Standard 22.3, read against the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions supplement listing, re-verified each January when the NAIC publishes the year's supplemental filing dates

In-scope processes.value: Preparation of the annual supplemental schedules and exhibits filed with or after the Annual Statement — Schedule F/S reinsurance detail, Schedule P loss development, Schedule DB derivatives, Supplemental Investment Risks Interrogatories, Reinsurance Attestation Supplement, Supplemental Compensation Exhibit, experience exhibits and Management's Discussion and Analysis

In-scope systems.value: Supplement modules in the blanks software, fed by the investment accounting system for Schedules D/DB, the reserving platform for Schedule P, the ceded accounting platform for Schedule F/S and the HRIS for the compensation exhibit

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Controller and re-approved each January after the NAIC supplement listing is refreshed; adding or dropping a supplement from the inventory requires a documented applicability test

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: March 1 supplements filed with the annual statement (Schedules F, P, DB, Reinsurance Attestation Supplement, Supplemental Compensation Exhibit); April 1 supplements (Management's Discussion and Analysis, the accident and health, credit and long-term care experience exhibits); August 1 internal control communications

Deadline reminders configured.value: One calendar task per supplement per entity with alerts at T-30, T-15 and T-5 calendar days to its own due date, since the April 1 supplements are routinely forgotten once March 1 has passed

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Each supplement as filed, its data extract, its cross-tie to the main blank, preparer and reviewer sign-off and the filing confirmation retained 7 years in the financial reporting repository under <company>-<year>-supplements

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any supplement filed after its own due date, any supplement that fails to tie to the main blank, and any applicability call reversed after filing is logged with cause and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Controller approves every late supplement, every re-filed supplement and every change to the supplement applicability inventory

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The full supplement inventory for each writing company for the statement year — every supplement judged applicable and every one judged not applicable, with its applicability basis

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every applicable supplement filed by its own due date and tying to the main blank to the dollar; any missing supplement, any untied schedule total, or any not-applicable call without a documented basis is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the test runs once per statement year in the window between the April 1 supplement date and the June 1 audited report date, covering both the March 1 and April 1 supplement sets

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared or reviewed any supplement in the tested year

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual supplements completeness and accuracy workpaper (inventory, applicability tests, cross-ties, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under <company>-<year>-supplements-test

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Supplement inventory with applicability basis, each filed supplement, its cross-tie to the blank and its confirmation, producible for a financial examination within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Controller answers examiner questions on supplement content; the Appointed Actuary answers Schedule P and reserve-development questions and the Reinsurance Manager answers Schedule F/S questions, with Regulatory Counsel clearing any restatement admission

checklist.step: Rebuild the supplement inventory and test applicability entity by entity
actions: Open the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions supplement listing and copy every supplement for the blank type into the inventory, with its own due date.

For each supplement record an applicability decision with a tested basis — for example the Medicare Supplement Insurance Experience Exhibit applies only if the entity wrote Medicare supplement premium, the Long-Term Care Experience Reporting Forms only if LTC is in force.
Take the tested value behind each decision from the blank itself (Exhibit 1 premium by line, Schedule T states) rather than from last year's inventory.
Name a preparer and an independent reviewer for every applicable supplement and publish the ownership matrix with the due dates.
checklist.done: the inventory shows every supplement with an applicability decision, a tested basis, a preparer, a reviewer and its own due date.

checklist.step: Build Schedule F or Schedule S reinsurance detail parts
actions: Extract the full ceded and assumed counterparty detail — NAIC company code or ID, name, domiciliary jurisdiction, authorized status, paid and unpaid recoverables, funds held and collateral by type.
Populate Schedule F Parts 1-3 (or Schedule S Parts 1-4 on a life blank) including the ageing of recoverables and the slow-paying reinsurer columns.
Recompute the provision for reinsurance in the schedule's own worksheet and confirm it equals the amount already booked on Page 3 of the blank.
Reconcile total ceded premium in the schedule to Exhibit 1 ceded premium and total recoverables to the Page 2 recoverable line.
Have the Reinsurance Manager review and sign the schedule before it goes into the pack.
checklist.done: Schedule F/S is complete by counterparty, the provision recomputes to the booked amount and totals tie to Exhibit 1 and Page 2.

checklist.step: Build the Schedule P loss development triangles
actions: Extract paid losses, case reserves, IBNR, defense and cost containment expense and earned premium by accident year and Schedule P line of business for the required ten-year history.
Populate Schedule P Parts 1-4 and confirm the current diagonal agrees to this year's Underwriting and Investment Exhibit paid and unpaid losses.
Agree every prior diagonal to the corresponding prior filed Schedule P, and where a figure moves, document the restatement reason on the schedule's support file.
Complete the Part 5 claim count development and the one-year and two-year reserve development lines, and explain adverse development above the materiality threshold in writing to the Chief Actuary.
Obtain the Appointed Actuary's sign-off that Schedule P is consistent with the Statement of Actuarial Opinion.
checklist.done: Schedule P ties to the current blank, agrees to prior filed diagonals except where restatement is documented, and is signed by the Appointed Actuary.

checklist.step: Build Schedule DB and the derivatives disclosures
actions: Extract every open derivative position at the statement date with counterparty, notional, fair value, hedge designation and the SSAP 86 hedge effectiveness result.

Populate Schedule DB Part A (options, caps, floors, collars, swaps and forwards), Part B (futures), Part C (replication transactions) and Part D (counterparty exposure), which is the ICP 15 Standard 15.7 disclosure in practice.
Confirm every position sits inside the board-approved derivatives use plan filed with the domiciliary state, and list any position that does not for the Chief Investment Officer.
Reconcile Schedule DB fair values to the investment accounting record and to the derivative balances on Pages 2 and 3.
Complete the Supplemental Investment Risks Interrogatories using the same holdings file, including the ten largest exposures and the asset concentration answers.
checklist.done: Schedule DB is complete by part, every position is inside the filed derivatives use plan, and values tie to the investment records and the blank.

checklist.step: Prepare the Reinsurance Attestation Supplement
actions: Have the Reinsurance Manager confirm in writing that no side agreement exists that would alter risk transfer on any treaty reflected in the statement.
Confirm risk-transfer documentation exists for every treaty accounted for as reinsurance, and that treaties failing risk transfer are on deposit accounting.
Sign the attestation with the Chief Executive Officer as the instructions require, dated on or before March 1.
File the signed attestation with the annual statement pack and retain the underlying treaty confirmations.
checklist.done: the attestation is signed by the CEO and CFO by March 1 and is supported by written treaty risk-transfer confirmations.

checklist.step: Prepare the Supplemental Compensation Exhibit
actions: Extract total compensation for the statement year for the officers and employees the instructions require, split into salary, bonus, deferred compensation and all other compensation.
Confirm the population matches the officers listed on the jurat page plus the highest-compensated individuals the instructions specify.
Reconcile total compensation to the general expense exhibit salary lines in the blank and explain the reconciling items.
Route the exhibit to the Chief HR Officer and the Controller for review before filing given its sensitivity, and restrict access in the repository.
checklist.done: the compensation exhibit covers the required population, reconciles to the general expense exhibit and is reviewed by the CHRO and Controller.

checklist.step: Prepare the line-of-business experience exhibits due April 1
actions: For each applicable exhibit — accident and health policy experience, credit insurance experience, long-term care experience reporting forms, Medicare supplement experience — extract earned premium, incurred claims and loss ratios by state and policy form.
Confirm the exhibit's premium total agrees to the corresponding Exhibit 1 line in the annual statement already filed on March 1.

Where a state-level loss ratio falls below a statutory minimum, notify the Product / Filing Actuary and the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager, because refund or rate action obligations follow.
File each exhibit by April 1 and capture the confirmation on the supplement inventory.
checklist.done: each applicable experience exhibit is filed by April 1, agrees to Exhibit 1 and has any sub-minimum loss ratio escalated.

checklist.step: Draft Management's Discussion and Analysis
actions: Draft the MD&A against the filed annual statement: premium and surplus movement, investment results, reserve development, liquidity and capital position, and material subsequent events.
Quote only figures that appear in the filed blank, and reference the page, exhibit or schedule each figure comes from.
Have the Controller and Chief Financial Officer review the narrative and the Corporate Secretary confirm the governance and subsequent-event statements.
File the MD&A with the domiciliary state by April 1 and capture the confirmation.
checklist.done: the MD&A is figure-tied to the filed blank, reviewed by the CFO and Corporate Secretary, and filed by April 1.

checklist.step: Cross-tie every supplement back to the main blank
actions: Build one cross-tie sheet listing each supplement, its key totals, the blank page/exhibit/schedule it must equal, and the actual difference.
Drive every difference to zero or to a documented, instruction-permitted reconciling item — never leave a difference described only as 'timing'.
Have a second preparer re-perform the three largest cross-ties and initial them.
Attach the cross-tie sheet to the supplement pack as the Controller's review evidence.
checklist.done: every supplement ties to its blank source at zero difference or with a documented reconciling item, independently re-performed on the three largest.

checklist.step: Run the independent review of each supplement
actions: For each supplement, the named reviewer re-checks the data extract parameters (period, entity, line of business filter) against the source system before reading the numbers.
Confirm the supplement uses the current-year form version from the instructions, not last year's template.
Record review comments on the supplement's review sheet and require the preparer to clear each one before sign-off.
Sign and date the review sheet; unsigned supplements do not go into the filing pack.
checklist.done: every applicable supplement carries a signed, dated review sheet with all comments cleared.

checklist.step: Assemble and file the March 1 supplement pack
actions: Assemble the supplements due March 1 with the annual statement export and upload them to the NAIC Financial Data Repository in the same submission where the instructions permit.
File separately with the domiciliary state any supplement the state demands directly, following the per-state matrix.
Capture the acceptance confirmation for each supplement and write its reference onto the inventory row.
Chase any supplement without a confirmation within 2 business days.
checklist.done: every March 1 supplement is submitted and carries a confirmation reference on the inventory.

checklist.step: Run the April 1 completeness sweep
actions: On March 20 run the inventory for applicable supplements with an April 1 due date and no draft in review.
Assign each open item to its named preparer with a hard internal date of March 27 so review time survives.
Confirm on April 1 that every April supplement carries a confirmation reference, and escalate any gap to the Controller the same day.
Record the sweep result on the inventory as the closing evidence for the April cycle.
checklist.done: on April 1 every April-due supplement is confirmed filed or escalated to the Controller with a recovery date.

checklist.step: Handle supplement corrections and re-filings
actions: Log any error found after filing with the supplement name, the affected figure and whether the main blank is also wrong.
Decide with the Statutory Reporting Manager whether the correction requires only a re-filed supplement or an amended annual statement as well.
Notify the domiciliary state in writing before re-filing, then re-file to the NAIC repository and every state that received the original.
Record the approval, the notice and the new confirmations against the tracker issue.
checklist.done: each supplement correction is assessed against the main blank, notified, re-filed everywhere and closed on the tracker with new confirmations.

checklist.step: Report supplement completeness to the Audit Committee
actions: Present the inventory outcome: supplements applicable, filed on time, filed late, and not applicable with the basis for each not-applicable call.
Report any supplement that failed to tie to the blank on first preparation and the fix applied.
Table adverse Schedule P development and any sub-minimum experience-exhibit loss ratio as named items rather than inside a summary.
Record the committee's acknowledgement in the minutes with the Corporate Secretary.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has the full supplement outcome, including adverse development and not-applicable bases, minuted by the Corporate Secretary.

checklist.step: Archive the supplement pack and its support
actions: Archive each filed supplement with its data extract, cross-tie sheet, review sheet and confirmation into <company>-<year>-supplements.
Apply the 7-year retention label and make the folder read-only outside the Controller.
Confirm the index allows retrieval by supplement name, entity and statement year for examination requests.
Close the supplement cycle on the close calendar.
checklist.done: the supplement pack, support and confirmations are archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by supplement name and year.

testing.step: Rebuild the supplement population independently
actions: Take the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions supplement listing for each blank type and build your own required-supplement list per entity.
Compare it to the preparer's inventory and investigate every supplement present in one and not the other.
Confirm the population covers both the March 1 and the April 1 supplement sets, since post-March-1 items are the common gap.
Sign the reconciled population as complete and date it.
testing.done: an independently built supplement list reconciles to the inventory with every difference investigated.

testing.step: Re-perform the applicability test on every not-applicable call
actions: For every supplement marked not applicable, read the instruction's own applicability trigger and test it against the filed blank — Exhibit 1 premium by line, Schedule T states, Schedule DB positions.
Treat any not-applicable call whose basis is 'not applicable last year' as an automatic exception.
Where a trigger is met, confirm the supplement was in fact prepared and filed and list it as a missing filing if not.
Capture the blank pages relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: every not-applicable call is independently tested against the instruction trigger and the filed blank.

testing.step: Draw the supplement sample
actions: Take 100% of Schedule F/S, Schedule P, Schedule DB, the Reinsurance Attestation Supplement and the Supplemental Investment Risks Interrogatories.
Select the remaining supplements to a minimum of eight further items using a recorded seed, ensuring at least two April 1 items are included.
Record the seed, the population size, the selection date and the entity coverage in the workpaper.
Add any supplement corrected or re-filed during the year as a mandatory sample item.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is drawn covering all major schedules, at least two April 1 items and every corrected supplement.

testing.step: Re-perform the Schedule F provision and counterparty ageing
actions: Extract the ceded recoverable detail independently and re-age the balances at the statement date to test the slow-paying reinsurer columns.
Recompute the provision for reinsurance from your own extract and compare it to both the schedule and the Page 3 booked provision.
Confirm each counterparty's authorized/certified status shown on the schedule matches the domiciliary state list at the statement date.
Log any difference above the workpaper tolerance as an exception with the surplus effect quantified.
testing.done: the provision and the recoverable ageing recompute to the filed schedule with every counterparty status verified.

testing.step: Reconcile Schedule P diagonals to prior filed schedules
actions: Pull the prior three filed Schedule P Parts 1-3 and compare every prior accident-year diagonal to the same cells in this year's filing.
List every restated cell and confirm a documented restatement reason exists on the support file.
Agree the current diagonal to the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit paid and unpaid losses in the filed blank.
Recompute the one-year and two-year reserve development lines from the triangles and compare to the filed figures.
testing.done: prior diagonals agree or are restatement-documented, the current diagonal ties to the blank, and development lines recompute.

testing.step: Verify Schedule DB positions against the derivatives use plan
actions: Select 15 derivative positions from the statement-date holdings and trace each to its Schedule DB part, notional, fair value and hedge designation.
Read the board-approved derivatives use plan as filed with the domiciliary state and confirm each sampled position is a permitted strategy and inside its limit.
Confirm the SSAP 86 hedge effectiveness evidence exists for every position designated as a hedge and that failed hedges are reported at fair value through surplus.
List any position outside the filed use plan as a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: every sampled derivative traces to Schedule DB, sits inside the filed use plan and has hedge-effectiveness evidence where designated.

testing.step: Re-perform the cross-ties between supplements and the blank
actions: Independently recompute each sampled supplement's key totals and compare them to the blank page, exhibit or schedule they must equal.
Treat any difference described only as timing, rounding or 'per instructions' without a named instruction paragraph as an exception.
Confirm the preparer's cross-tie sheet shows the same differences you found, since a clean sheet over a real difference is the more serious finding.
Capture the recomputation into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled supplement's totals independently tie to the blank, or the difference is logged with the preparer's sheet compared.

testing.step: Recompute supplement due dates and test timeliness
actions: Recompute each sampled supplement's own due date — March 1, April 1 or August 1 — from the instructions rather than from the inventory field.
Compare it to the confirmation date on the retained receipt and compute days late where applicable.
Confirm the attestation supplement carries both CEO and CFO signatures dated on or before March 1.
Tabulate every late supplement with its day count and the entity involved.
testing.done: every sampled supplement has an independently recomputed due date, a measured filing date and a verified signature date where required.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the entity, supplement, the defect and whether the main blank is also affected.
Assign a root cause — applicability rolled forward, April date missed after the March push, stale form version, untested extract filter — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date, and where a supplement was wrong or missing, require the re-filing to be completed and evidenced before the issue closes.
Carry every open exception into next year's supplement test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, where applicable, an evidenced re-filing.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the supplements test
actions: Compute the completeness rate (applicable supplements filed on time over applicable supplements) and the accuracy rate (supplements tying to the blank on first preparation).
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper reference behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared or reviewed no supplement in the year, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, any missing supplement and any Schedule P restatement to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with completeness and accuracy rates, a stated conclusion and an Audit Committee reporting date.
