checklist.step: Confirm the auditor appointment and record the awareness letter
actions: Confirm the Audit Committee has appointed the independent certified public accountant for the statement year by a minuted resolution naming the firm and the engagement partner.

Register the appointment with the domiciliary commissioner where the state requires notice, and diarise the awareness letter — the auditor's written statement of awareness of the state's requirements — within 6 months of the initial engagement.

Where the auditor changed, start the 5-business-day notification clock to the commissioner and prepare the explanatory letter due within 10 business days covering any disagreement in the prior 24 months.
File the resolution, awareness letter and any notification with the delivery evidence in the financial reporting repository.
checklist.done: the appointment is minuted, the awareness letter is on file, and any auditor change has been notified inside the 5- and 10-business-day windows.

checklist.step: Test auditor independence and lead partner rotation
actions: Obtain the firm's written independence confirmation for the statement year, naming the lead and concurring partners.

Count consecutive years served by the lead audit partner and the concurring partner against the 5-year limit and the 5-year cooling-off period, from the rotation register rather than the firm's assertion alone.

Extract from the procurement and accounts payable systems all non-audit fees paid to the firm and test each service against the prohibited-services list, particularly bookkeeping, actuarial services, internal audit outsourcing and management functions.
Confirm no member of the audit team took an employment position with the company within the 1-year cooling-off period.
Report the independence conclusion to the Audit Committee before fieldwork opens.
checklist.done: independence is confirmed in writing, rotation is within the 5-year limit, and no prohibited non-audit service has been engaged.

checklist.step: Verify audit committee composition and independence
actions: Test each audit committee member against the independence definition in the state's Model Audit Rule adoption, checking employment, consulting and related-party relationships.

Apply the premium-based thresholds: confirm whether the entity's direct written and assumed premium requires a majority-independent or wholly independent committee, and evidence the calculation from Exhibit 1 and Schedule F.
Confirm the committee's charter gives it responsibility for appointing, compensating and overseeing the auditor and a direct reporting line from the auditor.
Minute the annual independence determination for each member with the Corporate Secretary's certification.
checklist.done: each member's independence is tested against the state definition, the premium threshold is evidenced, and the determination is minuted.

checklist.step: Agree the audit plan, scope and PBC calendar
actions: Hold the planning meeting with the engagement partner and agree scope by entity, materiality, the significant risk areas (reserves, reinsurance recoverables, investment valuation, premium recognition) and the reliance planned on internal audit.
Load the prepared-by-client request list into the audit management platform with an owner and a due date per item, phased against the statutory close calendar.
Agree the interim and final fieldwork dates so the audit opinion can be signed with time to file by June 1.
Circulate the plan to the Appointed Actuary, Reinsurance Manager and Chief Investment Officer, since their areas carry the significant risks.
Have the Audit Committee approve the plan and the fee at its planning meeting.
checklist.done: an approved audit plan exists with per-item PBC owners and dates and fieldwork scheduled to clear June 1.

checklist.step: Deliver the PBC pack and manage open requests
actions: Upload each requested item against its PBC row with the source system, extract date and preparer named on the file.
Run the open-item report twice weekly during fieldwork and chase owners by name; items sitting over 5 business days go to the Controller.
Log every auditor question and its answer against the PBC row so the same question is not answered twice differently.
Refuse to supply unreviewed drafts — a document goes to the auditor only after its internal reviewer has signed it.
checklist.done: every PBC item is delivered from a named source with a signed internal reviewer, and no request is open beyond 5 business days at fieldwork close.

checklist.step: Support the reserve and reinsurance audit areas
actions: Give the auditor's actuarial specialist the reserve methodology memo, assumption basis, model version and the reconciliation from the model output to the booked reserves.
Walk the specialist through the asset adequacy analysis and the Statement of Actuarial Opinion, including any qualification or reliance stated.
Have the Reinsurance Manager provide treaty documentation and risk-transfer analysis for the treaties the auditor selects, with the collateral instruments behind the Schedule F provision.
Record every specialist observation and the company's response in the audit issue log.
checklist.done: the auditor's specialist has the reserve and reinsurance support requested and every observation is logged with a response.

checklist.step: Manage audit differences and the adjustment decision
actions: Maintain the schedule of audit differences with the amount, the affected blank line, whether it is factual, judgemental or projected, and the surplus effect of each.
Post every factual difference above the posting threshold rather than passing it, and document the rationale for anything passed.
Recompute the aggregate effect of unadjusted differences on surplus and on the RBC ratio, and take that recomputation to the Audit Committee.
Where an adjustment changes a figure already filed on March 1, open the amended-statement assessment with the Statutory Reporting Manager immediately.
Obtain the Audit Committee's decision on unadjusted differences in writing.
checklist.done: the differences schedule is complete, factual differences are posted, and the surplus and RBC effect of anything passed is Audit Committee approved.

checklist.step: Sign the management representation letter
actions: Read each representation against evidence rather than practice — related-party transactions, subsequent events, litigation and claims, reinsurance side agreements, and the completeness of the reserve data.
Obtain sub-representations in writing from the Appointed Actuary, Reinsurance Manager, General Counsel and Chief Investment Officer covering their areas before signing.
Confirm the litigation representation matches the legal letters received from external counsel.
Sign the letter with the Chief Executive Officer and date it the same day as the audit opinion.
checklist.done: the representation letter is supported by written sub-representations and signed by the CEO and CFO on the opinion date.

checklist.step: Receive the audit opinion and the audited statutory financial statements
actions: Read the opinion for its type — unmodified, qualified, adverse or disclaimer — and for any emphasis-of-matter or going-concern paragraph, and notify the CFO and Audit Committee chair the same day if it is anything but unmodified.
Agree the audited statutory financial statements page by page to the filed annual statement and explain every audit adjustment reflected.
Confirm the statements are presented on the statutory basis of the domiciliary state, with the permitted-practice reconciliation disclosed.
Have the Audit Committee accept the audited statements by minuted resolution before filing.
checklist.done: the opinion type is known and escalated where not unmodified, the statements agree to the filed blank plus adjustments, and the committee has accepted them.

checklist.step: File the audited financial report by June 1
actions: Assemble the audited financial report: the auditor's opinion, the audited statutory-basis statements, the notes and the required supplemental information.
File it with the domiciliary commissioner and with every other state whose Model Audit Rule adoption requires a direct filing, per the per-state matrix.
Where the June 1 date cannot be met, request a written extension from the domiciliary commissioner before June 1 with the reason and the committed date — never after.
Capture the filing confirmation for every state and write the reference onto the filing calendar row.
checklist.done: the audited report is filed with every state that requires it on or before June 1, or a pre-deadline written extension is on file.

checklist.step: Handle the adverse financial condition and material misstatement notifications
actions: Where the auditor determines the insurer does not meet its minimum capital and surplus requirement, or identifies a material misstatement, start the 5-business-day notification clock to the commissioner that day.
Draft the notification with General Counsel stating the determination, the amount and the company's response, and send it inside the 5 business days.
Confirm the auditor has independently made the notification the rule requires of them and that the two accounts do not conflict.
Log the determination date, the notification date and the day count on the tracker as permanent evidence.
checklist.done: any adverse determination is notified to the commissioner inside 5 business days with the day count evidenced.

checklist.step: Deliver the internal control communication and the management report by August 1
actions: Obtain from the auditor the communication of internal control related matters noted in the audit, identifying material weaknesses and significant deficiencies.
Test whether the entity exceeds the direct written and assumed premium threshold that triggers the Management's Report of Internal Control over Financial Reporting, evidencing the calculation.
Where triggered, prepare the management report covering the control framework used, the scope, and management's assertion, and have the CFO sign it.
File both with the domiciliary commissioner by August 1 and capture the confirmations.
checklist.done: the internal control communication and, where triggered, the signed management report are filed by August 1 with confirmations captured.

checklist.step: Remediate the reported control deficiencies
actions: Open a remediation record for every material weakness and significant deficiency with a named owner, a root cause and a target date inside the next audit cycle.
Agree the remediation test with the owner up front — what evidence will prove the control now operates — rather than after the fix.
Re-test each remediated control and record the result; a deficiency closes only on a passed re-test, not on a management assertion.
Report open and closed deficiencies to the Audit Committee at every meeting until all are closed.
checklist.done: every reported deficiency has an owner, a root cause, an agreed re-test and closes only on a passed re-test reported to the committee.

checklist.step: Hold the private sessions and close the audit cycle
actions: Schedule the Audit Committee's private session with the engagement partner without management present, as the Model Audit Rule contemplates, and minute that it took place.
Schedule the equivalent private session with the Chief Audit Executive and with the Appointed Actuary.
Minute the committee's conclusion on the audit, the unadjusted differences and the deficiency remediation plan.
Confirm the auditor's next-year engagement or the rotation decision and record the reasoning.
checklist.done: private sessions with the auditor, internal audit and the actuary are held and minuted, with the audit conclusion and next-year engagement recorded.

checklist.step: Archive the audit cycle evidence
actions: Archive the engagement and awareness letters, independence and rotation evidence, audit plan, differences schedule, representation letter, opinion, audited statements, filing confirmations and internal control communications into <company>-<year>-external-audit.
Apply the 7-year retention label and restrict edit rights to the Controller.
Confirm the index allows retrieval by entity, statement year and document type for a commissioner request.
Close the audit cycle on the filing calendar and open the next year's planning task.
checklist.done: the complete audit cycle record is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by entity and year.

testing.step: Build the population of audit cycles and required deliverables
actions: List every entity subject to the domiciliary state's Model Audit Rule adoption and, for each, the required deliverables: awareness letter, audited report, internal control communication, management report where triggered.
Confirm exemption claims — small-company premium exemptions granted by the commissioner — are supported by a written exemption order, not an internal judgement.
Reconcile the entity list to the Certificate of Authority register and the annual statement filings.
Sign the population as complete and date it.
testing.done: every in-scope entity and deliverable is listed, with each exemption supported by a written commissioner order.

testing.step: Re-perform the independence and lead partner rotation test
actions: Independently extract all payments to the audit firm and its affiliates for the year from procurement and accounts payable, by service description.
Classify each non-audit engagement against the prohibited-services list and challenge any described only as 'advisory'.
Recompute the lead and concurring partner tenure from the rotation register and the prior three engagement letters, not from the current year's letter alone.
List any prohibited service, any tenure over 5 years and any cooling-off breach as a reportable breach.
testing.done: non-audit fees are independently classified and partner tenure recomputed, with every breach reported.

testing.step: Test audit committee independence and the premium threshold calculation
actions: Recompute direct written plus assumed premium from Exhibit 1 and Schedule F/S and determine which Model Audit Rule committee-independence tier the entity falls into.
Test each committee member against the state's independence definition using the related-party disclosures and the D&O questionnaires.
Confirm the annual independence determination is minuted for the year under test and pre-dates the audit opinion.
Flag any entity whose premium moved it into a stricter tier without a corresponding committee change.
testing.done: the premium tier is independently recomputed and every committee member's independence is evidenced and minuted for the year.

testing.step: Draw the sample of audit deliverables and deadline events
actions: Take 100% of June 1 audited report filings, all 5-business-day notification events and all August 1 internal control communications.
Select 15 PBC items and 10 audit differences at random using a recorded seed.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
Add every control deficiency reported in the prior year that was claimed closed as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all filings and notification events plus seeded PBC items, differences and prior-year deficiency closures.

testing.step: Recompute the statutory clocks and prove the filings landed inside them
actions: For the audited report, compare the confirmation date to June 1 for every state that requires the filing and compute days late where applicable.

For each auditor change, count business days from the change decision to the commissioner notification against the 5-business-day limit and from notification to the explanatory letter against the 10-business-day limit.
For any adverse condition or material misstatement determination, count business days from the determination to the notification against the 5-business-day limit.
For the internal control communication and management report, compare the filing date to August 1.
Treat any extension claim as valid only where a written commissioner grant pre-dates the original deadline.
testing.done: every deadline is recomputed from the source event date and each filing is proved inside its clock or logged as late.

testing.step: Trace the audited statements to the filed annual statement
actions: Agree total assets, total liabilities, capital and surplus and net income in the audited statutory statements to the annual statement filed on March 1.
Reconcile every difference to a posted audit adjustment on the differences schedule and confirm each was assessed for an amended-statement requirement.
Confirm the audit opinion covers the same entity, statutory basis and period as the filed blank.
List any difference not explained by a documented adjustment as an exception.
testing.done: the audited statements reconcile to the filed blank line by line through documented adjustments, with amendment assessments evidenced.

testing.step: Re-perform the unadjusted differences assessment
actions: Recompute the aggregate surplus effect of the unadjusted differences and re-run the RBC ratio with those differences posted.
Compare your recomputation to the schedule taken to the Audit Committee and challenge any understated effect.
Confirm the committee's written decision to accept the unadjusted differences exists and pre-dates the opinion date.
Flag any factual difference above the posting threshold that was passed without a documented rationale.
testing.done: the surplus and RBC effect of unadjusted differences is independently recomputed and matched to a pre-opinion committee decision.

testing.step: Test the internal control deficiency remediation
actions: Pull every material weakness and significant deficiency reported in the current and prior year and its remediation record.
For each claimed closure, re-test the control yourself over a period after the fix date rather than reading the owner's assertion.
Confirm each open deficiency has a named owner, a root cause and a target date inside the next audit cycle.
List any deficiency closed without a passed re-test, and any repeated deficiency across two years, as findings in their own right.
testing.done: every claimed remediation is independently re-tested and repeat deficiencies are identified as separate findings.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the entity, the deliverable or clock breached, the day count and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause — late close feeding fieldwork, missed rotation tracking, unmonitored non-audit engagement, notification clock not started on determination day — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any missed statutory notification, require General Counsel to assess a voluntary disclosure to the commissioner.
Carry every open exception into next year's audit-cycle test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, where a clock was missed, a counsel-assessed disclosure decision.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the external audit compliance test
actions: Summarise results against the thresholds: June 1 filings on time, independence and rotation clean, statutory notifications inside their clocks, deficiencies owned and dated.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper reference behind each statement.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Finance and coordinated no part of the audit, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, any missed statutory clock and any repeat control deficiency to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with results against each threshold, a stated conclusion and an Audit Committee reporting date.

In-scope processes.value: Continuous maintenance of the obligation register: obligation discovery, calendar row creation with owner and due-date rule, reminder configuration, confirmation capture on submission, timeliness measurement and calendar change control across every jurisdiction the group is supervised in

In-scope systems.value: The obligation register and calendar of record, with reminders pushed to owners and confirmation artifacts indexed in the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Jurisdiction Filing Calendar Procedure — obligation discovery sources, row schema (jurisdiction, supervisor, obligation, legal basis, frequency, due-date rule, owner, channel, evidence type), quarterly horizon scan, change control and the monthly timeliness report

checklist.step: Define the register schema and the due-date rule format
actions: Set the mandatory fields for every row: jurisdiction, supervisor, legal entity, obligation name, legal basis citation, frequency, due-date rule, owner, submission channel, evidence type and retention period.

Require the due-date rule to be expressed as a computation from a period anchor (quarter end + 45 days, year end + 14 weeks, event date + 5 business days) so the calendar recomputes rather than being retyped.
Set the business-day convention per jurisdiction, including the local holiday calendar used when a due date falls on a non-business day.
Have the Head of Compliance approve the schema and lock it against ad-hoc field changes.
checklist.done: the register schema is approved, every field is mandatory, and due dates are held as computable rules with a stated business-day convention.

checklist.step: Build the jurisdiction and supervisor inventory
actions: List every legal entity and, for each, every supervisor it answers to — domiciliary and non-domiciliary state DOIs, the group-wide supervisor, and overseas regulators such as the Bermuda Monetary Authority, an EEA national competent authority under Solvency II, the Bank of England PRA or OSFI.
Take the state list from the Certificate of Authority register and the overseas list from the licences and branch registrations held by the Corporate Secretary.
Record for each supervisor the reporting portal, the company's registered filer credentials and the named regulatory contact.
Reconcile the inventory to the group structure chart so no subsidiary or branch is missing a supervisor.
checklist.done: every legal entity is mapped to every supervisor with its portal, credentials and contact, reconciled to the group structure chart.

checklist.step: Populate rows from the authoritative obligation sources
actions: Work source by source: the NAIC Annual Financial Reporting Checklist for each licensed state, the supervisor's own reporting calendar for each overseas regulator, and the group's holding-company registration requirements.
Create one row per obligation per entity per supervisor, pasting the citation and the source document date into the legal basis field.

Include event-driven obligations alongside periodic ones — material change notifications, adverse condition notifications, auditor change notifications, extraordinary dividend approvals — with their event-anchored due-date rules.
Reject any row whose legal basis cannot be cited; an obligation nobody can source is an obligation nobody can defend.
checklist.done: every obligation exists as a row with a cited legal basis and a dated source document, including event-driven notifications.

checklist.step: Assign a named owner and a backup to every row
actions: Assign each row to a named individual, not a team mailbox, and record a named backup.
Confirm each owner accepts the row in writing, including the due-date rule and the evidence they must capture.
Re-confirm ownership whenever a leaver or mover is notified by HR, and re-assign within 5 business days.
Publish the owner list quarterly so gaps are visible to the whole function.
checklist.done: every row has a named, accepting owner and backup, refreshed within 5 business days of any leaver or mover.

checklist.step: Configure reminders and escalation on every row
actions: Apply the standard lead times by obligation weight — T-30/T-15/T-5 business days for annual and supervisory returns, T-10/T-3 for quarterly, T-2 for event-driven rows.
Route reminders to the owner with the backup copied, and set the T-1 escalation to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Test each new row by forcing a reminder in a test period and confirming it reaches the owner's inbox.
Record the reminder configuration on the row so a missed reminder can be distinguished from an ignored one.
checklist.done: every row has tested reminders at its weight-appropriate lead times with a T-1 escalation to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly horizon scan for new and changed obligations
actions: Each quarter review the NAIC Annual Financial Reporting Checklist reissue, state DOI bulletin pages for every licensed state, and the published reporting calendars of each overseas supervisor.
Review IAIS and supervisory-college communications for changes to group-wide reporting expectations that flow into local returns.
Log every identified change on the horizon-scan log with the source, the date identified, the affected rows and the required calendar action.
Raise a change-control entry for each row created, re-dated or retired, and have the Head of Compliance approve retirements.
checklist.done: each quarter's scan is logged with sources and dates, and every resulting calendar change has an approved change-control entry.

checklist.step: Capture the confirmation artifact on every submission
actions: Require the row owner to attach the supervisor-issued artifact — portal receipt number, repository acceptance, acknowledgement email from the named regulatory contact, or courier proof of delivery — before the row can be marked filed.
Reject internal sent-mail records and unnumbered screenshots as evidence.
Name each artifact <entity>-<supervisor>-<obligation>-<period>-<yyyy-mm-dd> and index it by jurisdiction, supervisor and obligation.
Write the confirmation reference and the confirmed submission date back onto the row.
checklist.done: no row is marked filed without a supervisor-issued artifact indexed and referenced on the row.

checklist.step: Measure timeliness monthly against the computed due dates
actions: Extract all rows with a computed due date inside the month and join them to their confirmation dates.
Compute for each row on-time, late with day count, or not filed, applying the jurisdiction's business-day convention.
Break the result down by jurisdiction, supervisor, entity, owner and obligation type so repeat patterns surface.
Publish the monthly timeliness dashboard to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the Head of Compliance within 5 business days of month end.
checklist.done: a monthly timeliness measurement is published within 5 business days of month end, broken down by jurisdiction, supervisor and owner.

checklist.step: Work the open-row list before each due date
actions: Run the open-row report every Monday for rows due in the following 10 business days and confirm each owner has started.
For rows with no progress at T-5, take the row to the owner's manager the same day.
Where a supervisor's portal is unavailable or a data dependency has slipped, request a written extension from that supervisor before the due date and record the request and reply on the row.
Never mark a row closed on an intention to file — only on a captured confirmation.
checklist.done: every row due in the next 10 business days is progressed, escalated at T-5, or formally extended before its due date.

checklist.step: Reconcile the calendar to the licences held
actions: Each quarter compare the calendar's state coverage to the Certificate of Authority register, including states added, surrendered or suspended during the quarter.
Add calendar rows for every newly licensed state within 5 business days of the Certificate of Authority being issued, with its full filing set.
Retire rows only when the licence is formally surrendered and the final filing obligations are discharged, and record the surrender letter as the retirement source.
Report the reconciliation result to the Regulatory Reporting Manager with any state present in one register and not the other.
checklist.done: the calendar's state coverage reconciles to the Certificate of Authority register with new states added within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Control changes to calendar rows
actions: Require a change-control entry for every row created, re-dated, re-owned or retired, naming the source document and its date.
Block direct edits to the due-date rule field outside change control, since a quietly relaxed date is indistinguishable from a met deadline in the metrics.
Have the Head of Compliance approve every retirement and every relaxation of a due-date rule.
Keep the full change history on the row so a supervisor can be shown when and why a date moved.
checklist.done: every row change is under change control with a named source, approved retirements, and a visible change history.

checklist.step: Escalate and remediate a missed obligation
actions: On discovery of a missed filing, file it immediately and log the row with the computed due date, the actual filing date and the day count.
Have Regulatory Counsel assess whether a proactive disclosure to the supervisor is required and draft it where it is.
Establish the root cause — obligation never on the register, owner left, reminder never configured, dependency slipped — and fix the register, not just the filing.
Report the miss to the Compliance Committee with the fix and the retest commitment.
checklist.done: each missed obligation is filed, disclosed where counsel requires, root-caused into a register fix and reported to the Compliance Committee.

checklist.step: Attest the register's completeness annually
actions: Once a year require each row owner to confirm in writing that their rows are complete, correctly dated and correctly owned for the coming year.
Require each jurisdiction lead to confirm no obligation for their supervisor is absent from the register, citing the source they checked.
Sign the annual completeness attestation and file it with the register extract as at the attestation date.
Table the attestation and any qualification at the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: a signed annual completeness attestation exists, supported by per-owner and per-jurisdiction confirmations and a dated register extract.

checklist.step: Report timeliness and coverage to governance
actions: Report quarterly: rows due, on-time percentage, late rows with day counts, missed rows, extensions granted, and rows added or retired in the quarter.
Name repeat-offending obligations and owners rather than reporting an aggregate percentage only.
Report any supervisor late-filing notice, penalty or comment received in the quarter.
Record the committee's directions and carry them into the next quarter's calendar actions.
checklist.done: quarterly reporting names on-time rates, repeat offenders, supervisor notices and the committee's directions.

checklist.step: Archive the period's calendar evidence
actions: Archive per period the register extract, the confirmation artifacts, the horizon-scan log, the change-control entries and the timeliness dashboards.
Apply the 7-year retention label and make the archive read-only outside the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Confirm the index supports retrieval by jurisdiction, supervisor, entity, obligation and period.
Close the period on the register.
checklist.done: the period's register extract, artifacts, scan log and change entries are archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by jurisdiction and obligation.

testing.step: Extract the population of rows that fell due in the period
actions: Extract every calendar row with a computed due date inside the test period, with its jurisdiction, supervisor, entity, owner, due date and confirmation reference.
Recompute a sample of due dates from the row's stated rule and the period anchor to confirm the register's computation is right.
Reconcile the row count to the prior period's extract plus change-control additions minus approved retirements.
Sign the population as complete and date it.
testing.done: the due-row population is extracted, its due-date computations spot-checked, and its movement reconciled through change control.

testing.step: Test the register for completeness against external sources
actions: Pick five jurisdictions — at least two overseas — and build your own obligation list for each from the supervisor's published reporting calendar and the NAIC checklist entry.
Compare it to the register and list every obligation you found that has no row, which is the highest-value finding in this test.
Confirm each missing obligation against the entity's licence status so you are not reporting an obligation that does not apply.
Capture the supervisor source pages into the workpaper.
testing.done: five jurisdictions are independently rebuilt from supervisor sources and every unregistered obligation is listed with evidence.

testing.step: Draw and document the timeliness sample
actions: Take 100% of annual supervisory returns, all event-driven notification rows that triggered in the period, and all rows previously reported late.
Select 40 further rows at random using a recorded seed, stratified so every jurisdiction with more than ten rows is represented.
Record the seed, the population size, the stratification and the selection date in the workpaper.
Confirm the sample includes rows owned by at least ten different individuals.
testing.done: a reproducible, stratified sample covers all annual returns, event-driven rows, prior late rows and 40 seeded items.

testing.step: Verify the legal basis cited on each sampled row
actions: Open the cited source for each sampled row and confirm it actually imposes the obligation on that entity in that jurisdiction.
Check the source document date is current — a citation to a superseded checklist or a repealed instruction is an exception even where the date happens to still be right.
Confirm the frequency and due-date rule on the row match what the source says, including the business-day convention.
List any row whose legal basis field is blank, generic or unverifiable.
testing.done: each sampled row's legal basis is opened, confirmed current, and matched to the row's frequency and due-date rule.

testing.step: Trace sampled rows to a supervisor-issued confirmation
actions: Open the confirmation artifact for each sampled row and confirm it names the entity, supervisor, obligation and period.
Reject internal sent-mail, an owner's note or an unnumbered screenshot and mark the row unevidenced.
Where the supervisor's portal allows a filing-history lookup, re-open it and confirm the filing appears with the same date.
List every row marked filed in the register without a corroborated artifact.
testing.done: every sampled row is corroborated by a supervisor-issued artifact, with unevidenced rows listed.

testing.step: Recompute lateness and test the extension claims
actions: Recompute each sampled row's due date from its rule and anchor, applying the jurisdiction's holiday calendar, and compare to the confirmed submission date.
Compute days late for every row that missed, and compare your figure to the monthly timeliness dashboard for the same row.
For every extension claimed, read the supervisor's written grant and confirm the request pre-dated the original due date.
Flag any difference between your lateness calculation and the published dashboard as a metrics-integrity finding.
testing.done: lateness is independently recomputed for every sampled row, extensions are verified as pre-deadline, and dashboard differences are flagged.

testing.step: Test the horizon scan and change control
actions: Confirm a horizon scan was performed and logged in each quarter of the period with its sources named and dated.
Take five regulatory changes you can independently evidence occurred in the period and confirm each appears on the scan log and produced the right calendar action.
Pull every retired row and confirm a Head of Compliance approval and a source document exist for the retirement.
Pull every due-date rule relaxation and confirm it traces to a supervisor source, not to internal convenience.
testing.done: every quarter's scan is evidenced, five independently sourced changes are traced into the calendar, and all retirements and relaxations are approved and sourced.

testing.step: Reconcile calendar coverage to the licences held
actions: Take the Certificate of Authority register and the overseas licence and branch register at the period end and compare state and jurisdiction coverage to the calendar.
For every state licensed during the period, confirm its rows were created within 5 business days of the Certificate of Authority date.
For every surrendered licence, confirm final filing obligations were discharged before the rows were retired.
List any licensed jurisdiction with no calendar rows as a reportable control failure.
testing.done: calendar coverage reconciles to every licence held, with new-state rows created inside 5 business days and surrenders properly discharged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the jurisdiction, supervisor, obligation, days late or unregistered status, and the supervisory consequence.
Assign a root cause — obligation never registered, owner left without reassignment, reminder never configured, due-date rule wrong, dependency slipped — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any unregistered obligation, require the row to be created and evidenced before the issue closes.
Carry every open exception into the next period's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, for unregistered obligations, an evidenced new row.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the calendar test
actions: Compute the on-time rate against the 100% threshold and state separately the number of obligations found that were absent from the register.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper reference behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns no calendar row, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, the unregistered-obligation count and any supervisor penalty to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with an on-time rate, an unregistered-obligation count, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Producer Compliance Manager owns the Certificate of Authority register and the pre-write licence gate; the Chief Underwriting Officer owns the decision not to open a state/line until the gate clears

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 4 Standards 4.1-4.2 (licensing before carrying on insurance business) with ICP 7 Standards 7.7-7.8 (senior management accountability and documented delegation), read against the state's insurance code authority provisions and the current NAIC UCAA instructions for the application type in use

In-scope processes.value: Market entry gate: proposed state/line of business → Certificate of Authority and lines-of-authority check → UCAA expansion or corporate amendment application where coverage is missing → statutory deposit and registration conditions → release of the state/line into the underwriting and policy administration systems

In-scope systems.value: Certificate of Authority register of record holding the state, entity, authorised lines, effective and renewal dates, which feeds the state/line permission flags in the underwriting and policy administration platforms

Compliance procedure documented.value: Certificate of Authority Verification Procedure — market-entry intake, line-of-business mapping from the product's annual statement line to the state's authority wording, evidence capture from the DOI, UCAA route selection, deposit and condition checks, system enablement and the annual renewal cycle

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Chief Underwriting Officer; re-approved annually and whenever a state changes its lines-of-authority taxonomy or its UCAA participation

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per market entry — the gate must clear before the first solicitation in the state; renewal-dependent states carry an annual Certificate of Authority renewal date and fee, and corporate amendments must be filed before the change takes effect

Deadline reminders configured.value: Register reminders at T-90/T-60/T-30 days to each state's Certificate of Authority renewal or continuation date, plus a launch-gate alert to the Chief Underwriting Officer at T-30 days to any planned state/line go-live still unverified

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Certificate of Authority PDF as issued, the DOI company-lookup capture dated at verification, UCAA application and approval correspondence, deposit confirmations and the gate sign-off retained 7 years, and for the life of the licence plus 7 years in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any premium written in a state/line not on the Certificate of Authority, any lapsed renewal, and any system enablement made before the gate cleared is logged as a breach with the premium exposed and the remediation

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Regulatory Counsel signs off every unauthorised-business finding, the remediation route (rescission, non-renewal, self-report) and every decision to launch on a surplus lines or fronting basis instead

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every state/line combination carrying written premium in the period per Schedule T and the policy administration system, plus every market-entry gate decision recorded in the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any policy bound in a state/line not covered by a Certificate of Authority in force at the bind date is a fail and a reportable breach; any gate decision without a dated DOI evidence capture is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per market entry; the test runs quarterly over the quarter's bound premium by state/line and 100% of market-entry gate decisions made in the quarter

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have performed or approved any sampled gate decision

Evidence location for test results.value: Certificate of Authority coverage test workpaper (state/line premium population, register comparison, DOI re-verification, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under <quarter>-coa-coverage

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Certificate of Authority register extract with authorised lines and effective dates, the issued certificates and the gate sign-offs, producible for a market conduct examination within 5 business days

checklist.step: Take in the market-entry request and define the state/line scope
actions: Receive the entry request from the Insurance Product Manager naming the writing company, the target states, the product and its target launch date.
Record the product's annual statement line of business and the coverages it actually provides, because the coverage — not the product name — determines the authority needed.
Confirm the intended distribution channel and whether the risk is admitted, surplus lines or fronted, since each takes a different authority route.
Open a gate record per state with the entity, line, launch date and requester named.
checklist.done: one gate record exists per target state with entity, annual statement line, coverage description, channel and launch date.

checklist.step: Map the product's coverages to the state's lines-of-authority wording
actions: Open the state's insurance code authority classifications and list the exact line wording the state uses — states do not share a taxonomy, so 'casualty' in one is split across several in another.
Map each coverage in the product to the specific state line wording it falls under, and note any coverage that spans two lines.
Where a coverage is ambiguous, put the question in writing to the DOI's company licensing contact and record the question, date and answer on the gate record.
Record the mapped state line wording on the gate record — never the internal product line name alone.
checklist.done: every coverage in the product is mapped to named state line-of-authority wording, with ambiguities resolved in writing by the DOI.

checklist.step: Verify the Certificate of Authority in the state's own system
actions: Open the state DOI's company lookup for the writing company by NAIC company code and read the authority record as the state holds it, not as the internal register holds it.
Compare the authorised lines shown to the mapped line wording, and check the certificate's status is active with no suspension, restriction or condition.
Capture the lookup page to PDF named <state>-<entity>-coa-<yyyy-mm-dd> as the dated evidence behind the gate decision.

Pull the issued Certificate of Authority document from the licence file and confirm it agrees to the state's online record; where they differ, the state's record governs and the difference is investigated.
checklist.done: a dated DOI capture exists showing the entity's active authority and its lines, agreed to the issued certificate.

checklist.step: Decide the gate: clear, conditional or blocked
actions: Clear the gate only where every mapped line is on the active certificate for that entity with no restricting condition.
Mark the gate conditional where authority exists but the state imposes a condition — a deposit, a form filing, a holding-company registration — and name the condition and its owner.
Block the gate where any mapped line is missing, and route the state to the licence-expansion path rather than narrowing the product to fit.
Record the decision, decider, date and the evidence reference on the gate record.
checklist.done: every gate record carries a clear, conditional or blocked decision with a named decider, a date and an evidence reference.

checklist.step: Run the UCAA expansion application where authority is missing
actions: Select the right NAIC UCAA route: the Expansion Application for a new state, the Corporate Amendments Application for a change to an existing certificate, or the Primary Application for a newly formed entity.

Assemble the UCAA checklist items — the state-specific requirements page, audited financials, actuarial certification, biographical affidavits with third-party verification for officers and directors, plan of operation, and the certificate of compliance and certificate of deposit from the domiciliary state.
Confirm each biographical affidavit is within its validity window and that the third-party background verification is completed by an NAIC-accepted vendor.
Submit through the state's stated channel with the filing fee, and log the submission date and the state's expected review period on the gate record.
Track objections and respond inside the state's stated response window, escalating any question of financial condition to the Chief Financial Officer.
checklist.done: the correct UCAA application is submitted with a complete checklist and fee, and objections are tracked to a response inside the state's window.

checklist.step: Satisfy the deposit, registration and financial conditions
actions: Read the state's statutory deposit requirement for the lines applied for and confirm the amount, the eligible security types and the custodian arrangement the state accepts.
Place or increase the deposit and obtain the custodian's confirmation and the state's acknowledgement of the deposit.
Confirm any holding-company registration, surplus requirement or plan-of-operation condition is satisfied and evidenced.
Record the deposit reference and the condition evidence on the gate record and add the deposit to the annual statement Schedule E special deposits.
checklist.done: every deposit and financial condition is satisfied, acknowledged by the state and evidenced on the gate record and in Schedule E.

checklist.step: Record the granted authority in the register of record
actions: On receipt of the Certificate of Authority, enter the state, entity, NAIC company code, authorised lines in the state's own wording, effective date, expiry or continuation date and any condition.
Attach the certificate PDF and the DOI capture to the register row.
Notify Regulatory Reporting so the state's filing calendar rows are created within 5 business days.
Notify the Tax Manager so premium tax registration and the state's tax filing obligations are opened.
checklist.done: the register holds the new authority with its lines, dates, certificate and conditions, and Regulatory Reporting and Tax have been notified.

checklist.step: Enable the state/line in the underwriting and policy systems
actions: Open the state/line permission configuration and enable the combination only against a cleared gate record reference.
Set the enablement effective date to the Certificate of Authority effective date, never earlier, so no back-dated bind is possible.
Confirm the rating, forms and rules for that state are approved and in force before enablement, coordinating with the Product Filing Specialist.
Run a test quote and a test bind in the state to prove the configuration behaves, and keep the test evidence.
Confirm the system blocks binding in any state/line with no cleared gate.
checklist.done: the state/line is enabled from the certificate's effective date against a cleared gate, with a tested quote-and-bind and a proven block elsewhere.

checklist.step: Brief distribution and underwriting on what may be written
actions: Issue the underwriting authority bulletin naming the state, the entity, the exact lines authorised and the earliest bind date.
State explicitly which coverages are not authorised in that state and must be declined or placed on a surplus lines basis.
Publish the state's availability to appointed producers through the agent portal only after the gate has cleared and appointments are in place.
Record acknowledgement from each underwriting team lead.
checklist.done: underwriting and distribution have a dated bulletin naming authorised and unauthorised coverages, acknowledged by team leads.

checklist.step: Run the continuous unauthorised-business monitor
actions: Run a daily query joining bound policies to the Certificate of Authority register on entity, state, line and bind date.
Alert on any bind where no active authority covered the mapped line at the bind date, and on any bind in a state whose certificate was suspended.
Route each alert to the Producer Compliance Manager the same day with the policy number, premium and effective date.
Track alert closure and confirm no alert is closed without a documented resolution.
checklist.done: a daily monitor runs and every unauthorised-bind alert is routed same-day and closed with a documented resolution.

checklist.step: Remediate business written without authority
actions: Quantify the exposure: policies bound, premium written, losses paid and the period during which the state/line was open without authority.
Decide the remediation route with the Chief Underwriting Officer — rescind and rewrite on an authorised entity, place on surplus lines, non-renew at expiry — and never simply leave the book running.
Assess and, where required, make a self-report to the state DOI, drafting the disclosure and the corrective plan.
Confirm the system permission that allowed the bind is closed the same day and record the fix.
checklist.done: the exposure is quantified, a remediation route is chosen and executed, any required self-report is made and the system gap is closed same-day.

checklist.step: Run the annual Certificate of Authority renewal cycle
actions: Work the register's renewal reminders at T-90, T-60 and T-30 days, listing every state whose certificate requires an annual renewal, continuation filing or fee.
Submit each renewal with the state's required attachments — annual statement, corporate filings, fee — through the channel on the register row.
Capture the renewed certificate or the state's continuation confirmation and update the register's expiry date.
Escalate to the Head of Compliance any state within 30 days of expiry without a confirmed renewal, since a lapse stops new business immediately.
checklist.done: every renewal-dependent state is renewed with a captured confirmation and an updated register date, with lapses escalated at T-30.

checklist.step: File corporate amendments that change the certificate
actions: Identify every change that touches the certificate: name change, redomestication, merger, change of control, statutory home office address, or an added or dropped line.
File the UCAA Corporate Amendments Application with the domiciliary state and each licensed state as their instructions require, before the change takes effect.
Track approvals and update the register row only when the state has confirmed, not when the internal change was made.
Reissue the underwriting bulletin where the amendment changes what may be written.
checklist.done: every certificate-affecting corporate change is filed before it takes effect and the register is updated only on state confirmation.

checklist.step: Reconcile the register to written premium each quarter
actions: Take the quarter's direct written premium by state and annual statement line from Schedule T and the policy administration system.
Compare each populated state/line to the register and confirm active authority covered the whole quarter.
Investigate every state/line with premium and no authority, and every state with authority and no premium — the latter may signal a licence worth surrendering.
Report the reconciliation to the Chief Underwriting Officer and the Controller, who relies on it for the Schedule T licence cross-check.
checklist.done: each quarter's premium by state/line reconciles to the register with every unmatched combination investigated and reported.

checklist.step: Archive the gate and licence evidence
actions: Archive per state the gate record, the line-of-authority mapping, the dated DOI captures, the UCAA application and approval, deposit confirmations and the issued certificate.
Apply retention of the life of the licence plus 7 years so surrendered-state records survive.
Confirm the index supports retrieval by state, entity, NAIC company code and line of authority.
Close the gate record and link it to the register row.
checklist.done: the state's full licensing evidence is archived under life-of-licence-plus-7-years retention and linked to its register row.

testing.step: Build the population of state/line combinations carrying premium
actions: Extract every policy bound in the quarter with writing entity, state, annual statement line, bind date, effective date and written premium.
Aggregate to unique entity/state/line combinations and reconcile the premium total to Schedule T for the same period.
Add every market-entry gate decision recorded in the quarter, cleared, conditional or blocked, as a second population.
Sign both populations as complete and date them.
testing.done: the bound-premium population reconciles to Schedule T and every gate decision in the quarter is captured.

testing.step: Reconcile every populated state/line to an authority in force at the bind date
actions: Join each entity/state/line combination to the Certificate of Authority register on the line wording and test the certificate was active across the whole quarter.
Test the earliest bind date in each combination against the certificate's effective date — a bind one day early is the same breach as a bind a year early.
List every combination with premium and no covering authority as an automatic reportable breach, with the premium quantified.
Check for suspended or conditioned certificates that were treated as fully active.
testing.done: every populated combination is matched to an authority in force across the bind dates, or is listed as a quantified breach.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of state/lines entered for the first time in the quarter and 100% of gate decisions recorded in the quarter.
Select 25 further established state/line combinations at random using a recorded seed, weighted to the highest premium.
Record the seed, the population size and the selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every state whose certificate renewed during the quarter as a mandatory item.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all new entries, all gate decisions, all renewals and 25 seeded established combinations.

testing.step: Re-verify authority in the state's own system for each sampled row
actions: Open each sampled state's DOI company lookup by NAIC company code and read the authority record yourself before opening the register row.
Compare the lines the state shows to the register's recorded lines and to the product coverages actually written.
Treat 'right authority, wrong line wording on the register' as an exception, since the register drives the system permissions.
Capture each lookup page into the workpaper with the date of capture.
testing.done: each sampled state's authority is independently re-verified in the DOI system and captured, with wording differences logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the coverage-to-line-of-authority mapping
actions: For ten sampled products read the policy forms actually in use and map the coverages to the state's statutory line classifications independently of the gate record.
Focus on coverages that commonly straddle lines — inland marine within property, mechanical breakdown, cyber, and any embedded liability extension.
Compare your mapping to the gate record's; a coverage written under an authority that does not reach it is unauthorised business even where the certificate looks broad.
Record the legal reasoning for each difference in the workpaper.
testing.done: ten products are independently re-mapped to statutory line classifications with every difference reasoned and recorded.

testing.step: Test the system permission gate against the register
actions: Extract the state/line permission configuration from the underwriting and policy administration platforms with the enablement effective dates.
Compare each enabled combination to the register and list any enabled with no authority or enabled before the certificate's effective date.
Attempt a test quote in a deliberately unauthorised state/line combination in the test environment and confirm the system blocks the bind.
List any enablement made without a cleared gate record reference.
testing.done: system permissions reconcile to the register, no enablement pre-dates its certificate, and the block on unauthorised combinations is proven by test.

testing.step: Test the deposits, conditions and renewals behind the sampled certificates
actions: For each sampled state, read the statutory deposit requirement and confirm the deposit held, per the custodian confirmation and Schedule E special deposits, meets it at the quarter end.
Confirm every condition attached to the certificate — plan of operation, holding-company registration, surplus maintenance — is evidenced as satisfied.
For each renewal in the quarter, compare the renewal confirmation date to the certificate's expiry date and flag any gap where the licence lapsed.
Quantify any premium bound during a lapse as a breach.
testing.done: deposits and conditions are verified as satisfied at quarter end and every renewal is proven to have preceded expiry.

testing.step: Test the daily unauthorised-business monitor
actions: Confirm the daily monitor ran every business day in the quarter and retrieve its alert log.
Seed a known unauthorised combination in the test environment and confirm the monitor raises it, proving the rule works rather than assuming it.
Compare the monitor's alerts to the breaches you found independently — breaches the monitor missed are a control design finding.
Confirm every alert was routed same-day and closed with a documented resolution.
testing.done: the monitor is proven to run daily and to detect a seeded breach, with any missed breach raised as a design finding.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the entity, state, line, policies affected, premium exposed and whether losses were paid.
Assign a root cause — coverage mis-mapped to a line, system enabled before the certificate date, renewal lapsed, register wording stale — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any unauthorised business, require Regulatory Counsel's self-report assessment before the issue closes.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, quantified premium exposure, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a counsel self-report assessment where required.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the authority coverage test
actions: Compute the breach count and the premium written without authority against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper reference behind each breach.
Have the independent reviewer, who approved none of the sampled gate decisions, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, the exposed premium and any self-report to the Compliance Committee and the Chief Underwriting Officer, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with a breach count, quantified exposed premium, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date.
