checklist.step: Take in the contracting request and capture the producer's identifiers
actions: Open the contracting request from the Agency Relations Manager and record the producer's legal name, National Producer Number (NPN), tax identification number, resident state and agency affiliation.
Record which entity, products and states the producer is being contracted to sell, taken from the distribution request rather than assumed from the agency's other producers.
Confirm whether the producer is an individual or a business entity, since business entities need their own licence and a designated responsible licensed producer.
Reject the request back to the Agency Relations Manager where the NPN is missing — every downstream check keys on it.
checklist.done: the producer record holds NPN, legal name, resident state, entity type and the exact entity/product/state scope requested.

checklist.step: Pull the Producer Database report from NIPR
actions: In NIPR Gateway open the Producer Database (PDB) and run the report by NPN for the producer.
Read for every state on the request: licence status (active, inactive, expired, suspended, revoked), licence class, lines of authority, resident or non-resident, original issue date and expiry date.
Read the Regulatory Information Retrieval System (RIRS) section for administrative actions and the appointment history section for prior carrier terminations.
Save the PDB report to PDF named <NPN>-pdb-<yyyy-mm-dd> as the dated evidence behind the eligibility decision — a screen glance is not evidence.
Run the report again if it is more than 30 days old at the point of decision.
checklist.done: a dated PDB report exists per producer covering licence status, class, lines, residency, expiry and RIRS actions for every requested state.

checklist.step: Match the lines of authority to the products the producer will sell
actions: Map each product in scope to the line of authority the state requires — life, accident and health, variable life and variable annuity, property, casualty, personal lines — and record the mapping per state.
Compare the mapped lines to the lines the PDB shows as active in that state, per state, not in aggregate.

Where the product is a variable annuity or variable life contract, confirm the producer also holds the required securities registration on FINRA's CRD and is associated with the distributing broker-dealer.
Record any state where the producer is licensed but lacks the line, and hold that state out of scope rather than contracting broadly.
checklist.done: every product/state pairing is matched to an active line of authority on the PDB, with variable business also matched to a securities registration.

checklist.step: Test residency and non-resident licence coverage
actions: Identify the producer's resident state from the PDB and confirm the resident licence is active with the required lines.
For every other state in scope confirm a non-resident licence exists — a resident licence does not travel, and countersignature or business-entity requirements may also apply.
Where a state is missing, submit the non-resident application through NIPR Gateway's non-resident licensing transaction with the fee and track it to issuance.
Confirm the resident licence remains active while the non-resident licences depend on it, since a resident lapse invalidates them.
checklist.done: the resident licence is active and every in-scope state has an active licence or a tracked non-resident application, with dependency understood.

checklist.step: Review the regulatory action and financial-crime screening
actions: Read every RIRS action on the PDB — state, date, reason code, disposition — and obtain the underlying state order for any action involving fraud, misappropriation or misrepresentation.
Run the sanctions and adverse-media screen on the producer's name and identifiers and clear any hit as a true or false match with the rationale recorded.
Confirm no felony conviction involving breach of trust or dishonesty exists that would require federal written consent before employment in the business of insurance.
Escalate every adverse finding to the Head of Compliance with a written recommendation rather than deciding at coordinator level.
checklist.done: every regulatory action and screening hit is read, dispositioned in writing and, where adverse, escalated to the Head of Compliance.

checklist.step: Confirm the training prerequisites for the products in scope
actions: For annuity products confirm the producer has completed the state's one-time annuity best-interest training and the carrier's product-specific training before the first solicitation.
For long-term care products confirm the state's initial LTC training and its ongoing refresher requirement.
Confirm anti-money-laundering training is current where the products are covered financial products, and record the completion date.
Store each completion certificate against the producer record and set the refresher reminder from the completion date.
checklist.done: every state-mandated and carrier-mandated training for the in-scope products is completed and evidenced before solicitation.

checklist.step: Confirm the errors and omissions cover and the agency contract
actions: Obtain the current E&O certificate showing carrier, limits, retention and policy period, and confirm the limits meet the carrier's minimum and any state requirement.
Diarise the E&O expiry and set a reminder at T-30 days, since lapsed cover suspends the right to solicit under the agency contract.
Confirm the producer or agency contract is executed, with the commission schedule, the states and products in scope, and the compliance obligations attached.
Where the producer sells through a business entity, confirm the entity's own licence and its designated responsible licensed producer are recorded.
checklist.done: current E&O and an executed contract are on file with expiry reminders set and any business entity licence recorded.

checklist.step: Record the eligibility decision and set the sell flag
actions: Record the decision — eligible, eligible with restrictions, or declined — naming the states, products and lines it covers and the PDB report it relies on.
Set the producer's sell flag per state and product so the flag, not a person's memory, controls what can be submitted.
Where the decision is restricted, state the restriction in terms the system can enforce, such as a state or product exclusion.
Record the decider and date, and notify the Agency Relations Manager and the Distribution Operations Manager.
checklist.done: an eligibility decision with named state/product scope is recorded, enforced by the sell flag, and notified to Distribution.

checklist.step: Enforce the pre-solicitation block in the submission systems
actions: Configure the new-business intake so an application cannot be accepted unless the submitting producer's NPN carries an eligible sell flag for that state and product on the application date.
Block agent portal access to product materials and quoting for states and products outside the producer's eligibility.
Test the block with a deliberately ineligible NPN in the test environment and retain the evidence.
Confirm the block applies to applications arriving by every channel — portal, email, agency upload and API — since one open channel defeats the control.
checklist.done: the submission block is configured, tested against an ineligible NPN and proven to cover every intake channel.

checklist.step: Run the daily re-verification sweep against NIPR
actions: Run the daily NIPR data reconciliation feed against the full active producer file and pull status changes: expirations, cancellations, suspensions, revocations, line-of-authority changes and new RIRS actions.
Flip the sell flag to no-sell the same day for any producer whose licence is no longer active in a state, per state rather than globally.
Alert the Agency Relations Manager the same day so in-flight business is redirected to an eligible producer.
Log every status change and the action taken on the producer record.
checklist.done: the daily sweep runs, status changes flip the sell flag per state the same day, and Distribution is alerted for in-flight business.

checklist.step: Work the licence renewal and continuing-education pipeline
actions: Work the T-90, T-60 and T-30 renewal reminders and confirm each producer's CE hours are satisfied in the resident state, since CE shortfalls block renewal.
Where the carrier holds the renewal responsibility, submit through NIPR Gateway's licence renewal transaction with the fee before the expiry date.
Track each renewal to a confirmed status change on the PDB, not to a submitted transaction.
Escalate to the Producer Compliance Manager any producer inside 30 days of expiry with an unresolved CE shortfall.
checklist.done: every renewal is worked to a confirmed PDB status change before expiry, with CE shortfalls escalated at T-30.

checklist.step: Handle a producer with an adverse regulatory history
actions: Read the state order behind the action and establish what conduct it concerned, what sanction was imposed and whether conditions remain in force.
Decide contract, contract with conditions (supervision, restricted products, business review) or decline, and record the reasoning in writing.
Where conditions are imposed, name the supervisor, the review frequency and the review evidence, and set a review date.
Notify the Head of Distribution of the decision and any condition that limits what the producer may sell.
checklist.done: each adverse-history producer has a written, reasoned decision with any supervision conditions named, evidenced and dated for review.

checklist.step: Remediate business taken by an ineligible producer
actions: Quantify the exposure: applications taken, policies issued, premium and commission paid while the producer was unlicensed or out of line.
Decide the policyholder treatment with the Chief Underwriting Officer — the policies generally remain in force to protect the insured — and the commission treatment, which usually requires recovery.
Assess and, where required, self-report to the affected state DOI with the corrective plan and the commission disposition.
Suspend the commission payments in the commission platform the same day and close the system gap that allowed the submission.
checklist.done: the exposure is quantified, commissions are suspended and dispositioned, any self-report is made and the system gap is closed same-day.

checklist.step: Report producer eligibility health to Distribution and Compliance
actions: Report monthly: producers contracted, eligibility declines, adverse-history approvals with conditions, no-sell flags raised, renewals missed and business blocked at intake.
Name repeat agencies whose producers fail verification, since the pattern usually sits at agency level.
Report any unlicensed-solicitation breach separately with the premium and commission involved.
Take the report to the Compliance Committee and the Head of Distribution and record the actions agreed.
checklist.done: monthly eligibility metrics, agency-level patterns and breaches are reported to Compliance and Distribution with agreed actions recorded.

checklist.step: Archive the producer eligibility file
actions: Archive per producer the dated PDB reports, the line-of-authority match, screening dispositions, training certificates, E&O certificates, the contract and the eligibility decisions.
Apply retention of 7 years after the relationship ends so the file survives termination.
Confirm the index supports retrieval by NPN, producer name, agency and state for examination requests.
Refresh the archived PDB report at each annual re-verification rather than relying on the onboarding copy.
checklist.done: each producer's eligibility file is archived under 7-years-after-termination retention, indexed by NPN and refreshed annually.

testing.step: Build the producer population from business actually submitted
actions: Extract every application submitted and every policy issued in the period with the submitting producer's NPN, the state, the product and the application date.
Add every producer who received a commission payment in the period from the commission platform, since commission without submitted business is its own signal.
Reconcile the producer count to the active producer file in the producer management system and investigate producers paid but not on file.
Sign the population as complete and date it.
testing.done: the population covers every producer who submitted business or was paid, reconciled to the active producer file.

testing.step: Reconcile every submission to an eligible licence at the application date
actions: Join each application to the producer's licence history and test that an active licence with the matching line existed in that state on the application date.
Test against the licence history rather than today's status, since a producer active today may have been expired then.
List every application taken without a covering licence or line as an automatic breach, quantifying premium and commission.
Separate breaches caused by expiry from those caused by a missing line, because the fixes differ.
testing.done: every application is matched to a licence active on its own date, with breaches quantified and classified by cause.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of producers contracted in the period, 100% of adverse-history approvals and 100% of producers selling annuity or variable products.
Select 40 further producers at random using a recorded seed, weighted to the highest submitted premium.
Record the seed, the population size and the selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every producer whose sell flag flipped to no-sell during the period as a mandatory item.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all new contracts, adverse-history approvals, annuity and variable sellers, no-sell flips and 40 seeded producers.

testing.step: Re-pull the PDB report and re-perform the eligibility judgement
actions: Run a fresh PDB report by NPN for each sampled producer and reach your own eligibility conclusion per state and product before opening the file.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded decision; a right decision resting on a stale or missing PDB report is still an exception.
Confirm the retained PDB report was dated within 30 days of the eligibility decision.
Capture the fresh report into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled producer's eligibility is independently re-concluded from a fresh PDB report and compared to the recorded decision.

testing.step: Re-perform the line-of-authority to product mapping
actions: For 20 sampled producer/product pairings, map the product to the state's required line of authority yourself from the state's licence class definitions.
Compare to the licence lines on the PDB at the application date, per state.
For variable annuity and variable life sales, confirm the securities registration on FINRA CRD and the broker-dealer association were in force at the sale date.
Treat a life-only licence used for an annuity sale in a state requiring a separate line as a breach, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: 20 producer/product pairings are independently mapped and matched to lines in force at the sale date, including securities registration.

testing.step: Test the training prerequisites behind annuity and long-term care sales
actions: For every sampled annuity sale, confirm the state's annuity best-interest training and the carrier's product-specific training were completed before the application date, not merely before the test.
For long-term care sales, confirm the initial training and the refresher cycle are both satisfied.
Trace each completion to a dated certificate in the learning system rather than a status field.
List any sale preceding its required training as an exception with the policy identified.
testing.done: every sampled annuity and LTC sale is preceded by dated, certificated training completions.

testing.step: Test the intake block and the daily re-verification sweep
actions: Attempt a test submission in the test environment using an NPN with no eligible sell flag and confirm every intake channel rejects it.
Confirm the daily NIPR reconciliation ran on every business day in the period and retrieve its change log.
Take ten producers whose licences expired or were suspended during the period and check how many business days elapsed before the sell flag flipped — anything beyond same-day is an exception.
Compare the sweep's detections to the breaches you found independently and raise anything missed as a control design finding.
testing.done: the intake block is proven across channels and the sweep is proven to run daily and flip flags same-day, with misses raised as design findings.

testing.step: Test the adverse-history approvals and their conditions
actions: Pull every producer approved despite a RIRS action and read the underlying state order held on file.
Confirm the Head of Compliance's written reasoning exists and pre-dates the contract date.
Where supervision conditions were imposed, test that the named supervisor performed the reviews at the stated frequency and that the review evidence exists.
List any conditional approval running without evidenced supervision as an exception.
testing.done: every adverse-history approval has a pre-dated written rationale and, where conditional, evidenced supervision at the stated frequency.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the producer NPN, agency, state, product, applications affected, premium and commission paid.
Assign a root cause — stale PDB report, line mismatch, expiry not swept, training gap, channel bypassing the intake block — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, for unlicensed solicitation, require Regulatory Counsel's self-report assessment and a commission recovery decision before closure.
Carry every open exception into the next period's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, quantified premium and commission, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a counsel assessment where required.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the producer eligibility test
actions: Compute the breach count and the premium and commission written by ineligible producers against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper reference behind each breach.
Have the independent reviewer, who approved none of the sampled eligibility decisions, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, the exposed premium and commission and any self-report to the Compliance Committee and the Head of Distribution, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with a breach count, exposed premium and commission, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Producer Licensing Coordinator files every appointment and termination transaction and owns the statutory clock on each; the Producer Compliance Manager owns the for-cause reporting decision

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 22 Standard 22.3 (risk-based intermediary due diligence) with ICP 18, read against each state's adoption of the NAIC Producer Licensing Model Act sections 16 and 17 — appointment within 15 days of the agency contract or the first application submitted, and termination notice within 30 days of the effective date — re-verified per state annually and on any DOI bulletin

In-scope processes.value: Event-driven appointment and termination processing: contract execution or first application → appointment filing through NIPR → state confirmation → annual appointment renewal; and termination decision → state notice → producer notice → for-cause reporting and supplemental information

In-scope systems.value: NIPR Gateway appointment, termination and appointment-renewal transactions, with the producer management system holding the appointment register and the commission platform keyed to appointment status

Compliance procedure documented.value: Appointment and Termination Processing Procedure — trigger definitions per state (appointment-prior versus just-in-time), the 15-day and 30-day clock rules, effective-date and back-dating rules, producer notice within 15 days of the state notice, for-cause criteria and the supplemental-information duty

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Head of Distribution; the per-state clock and trigger matrix is re-approved annually against the states' current statutes and NIPR transaction rules

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Appointment filed within 15 days of the earlier of the agency contract date or the first application submission; termination notice to the state within 30 days of the effective date; notice to the producer within 15 days of notifying the state; supplemental information to the state within 30 days of it becoming known; annual appointment renewals per each state's renewal cycle and invoice

Deadline reminders configured.value: Per-transaction clocks that start on the trigger event date with alerts at day 5 and day 10 of the 15-day appointment window and at day 10 and day 20 of the 30-day termination window, escalating to the Producer Compliance Manager one day before expiry

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Trigger evidence (contract date or first application date), the NIPR transaction confirmation with its date, the state's appointment or termination confirmation, the producer notice with proof of delivery and any for-cause report retained 7 years after the relationship ends

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every appointment filed beyond 15 days, every termination notice beyond 30 days, every producer notice beyond 15 days and every missed for-cause report is logged with the day count, the state and the disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Producer Compliance Manager signs off every late appointment or termination filing, every for-cause characterisation and every decision to report or not report conduct to a state

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every appointment trigger in the period (contract executions and first applications by unappointed producers) and every termination effective in the period, by producer, entity and state

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of appointments filed within 15 days of the trigger and 100% of terminations notified within 30 days of the effective date, with producer notice inside 15 days; any single breach of a statutory window is a fail reported to the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; the test runs monthly over that month's appointment triggers and termination events, with 100% coverage of for-cause terminations

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have filed any sampled appointment or termination transaction

Evidence location for test results.value: Appointment and termination timeliness workpaper (trigger population, clock recomputation, NIPR confirmations, notice evidence, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under <month>-appointments-terminations

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-transaction pack — trigger evidence, NIPR confirmation, state confirmation, producer notice with delivery proof and any for-cause report — producible for a DOI producer-licensing inquiry within 3 business days

Regulator response path.value: Producer Compliance Manager answers DOI appointment and termination inquiries; Regulatory Counsel clears every for-cause report and any response conceding a missed statutory window, and handles producer disputes over a for-cause characterisation

checklist.step: Maintain the per-state appointment trigger and clock matrix
actions: Build one row per state recording whether appointment must precede solicitation or may be filed just-in-time after the first application, the days allowed, and whether the state permits an effective date back-dated to the trigger.
Record the termination window, the producer-notice window, the state's for-cause reason codes and its supplemental-information duty.
Cite the statute or DOI bulletin behind every field and record the date the source was read.
Have the Head of Compliance approve the matrix annually and any interim change under change control.
checklist.done: every state has a sourced row covering appointment trigger, days allowed, back-dating, termination and notice windows and for-cause codes.

checklist.step: Detect the appointment trigger the day it happens
actions: Run a daily job that identifies the earlier of two events per producer/entity/state: the executed agency or producer contract date, and the first application submission date by an unappointed producer.
Create an appointment task on the trigger date with the state's day count from the matrix and the computed statutory due date on its face.
Attach the trigger evidence to the task — the executed contract PDF or the application record with its submission timestamp.
Route the task to the Producer Licensing Coordinator the same day and alert the Agency Relations Manager.
checklist.done: every trigger creates a same-day task carrying the trigger evidence, the state's day count and a computed statutory due date.

checklist.step: Confirm eligibility before filing the appointment
actions: Re-run the PDB report by NPN and confirm the licence is active in the appointing state with the lines the appointment covers.
Confirm the producer's sell flag is eligible and that no no-sell condition applies to that state or product.
Confirm the appointing entity holds a Certificate of Authority for the line in that state, because an appointment cannot outrun the carrier's own authority.
Where any check fails, hold the appointment and escalate to the Producer Compliance Manager the same day rather than filing and fixing later.
checklist.done: the appointment is filed only after licence, line, sell flag and carrier authority are all confirmed for that state.

checklist.step: File the appointment transaction through NIPR
actions: In NIPR Gateway open the appointment transaction, select the appointing company by NAIC company code and the state, and enter the producer's NPN.
Select the lines of authority the appointment covers and set the effective date to the trigger date where the state permits back-dating, otherwise to the earliest date the state allows.
Submit with the state's appointment fee and capture the transaction confirmation number and date.
Track the transaction to the state's acceptance on the PDB appointment section — a submitted transaction is not an appointment.
Write the confirmation number, submission date and confirmed effective date onto the appointment register row.
checklist.done: the appointment is submitted with fee, confirmed on the PDB, and its confirmation number and effective date are on the register.

checklist.step: Prove the 15-day clock was met on every appointment
actions: For each completed appointment compute days elapsed from the trigger date to the NIPR submission date using the state's day-counting convention.
Compare it to the state's allowed window from the matrix and mark the row on time or late with the day count.
Escalate every late row to the Producer Compliance Manager the day it is identified, with the applications the producer submitted in the gap.
Attach the trigger evidence and the NIPR confirmation to the row as the timeliness proof.
checklist.done: every appointment row carries a computed day count against the state's window with trigger and confirmation evidence attached.

checklist.step: Work the daily appointment ageing report
actions: Run the open-appointment ageing every business day showing days elapsed against the state's window per task.
Chase every task at day 5 and day 10, and personally clear anything at day 14 rather than letting the clock expire.
Where the producer's licence is the blocker, decide the same day whether to withdraw the appointment and redirect the in-flight business to an appointed producer.
Report any expired window to the Head of Compliance the day it expires.
checklist.done: no appointment task passes its statutory window without either a filing or a same-day escalation to the Head of Compliance.

checklist.step: Run the annual appointment renewal cycle
actions: Work each state's appointment renewal cycle and reconcile the state's renewal invoice against the appointment register before paying it.

Identify producers who should not be renewed — inactive, terminated in fact but not on the register, or no longer licensed — and remove them before the invoice is paid, since renewing a dead appointment both wastes fees and misstates the record.
Submit the renewal through NIPR Gateway with the fee and capture the confirmation.
Confirm the renewed appointments appear on the PDB and update the register's renewal dates.
checklist.done: each state's renewal is reconciled to the register, non-renewals are removed first, and renewed appointments are confirmed on the PDB.

checklist.step: Take in the termination decision and classify it
actions: Record the termination request with the producer NPN, the entities and states affected, the effective date and the reason narrative.
Classify the termination as without cause or for cause, applying the state's own reason codes rather than an internal label.
Route every proposed for-cause classification to the Producer Compliance Manager and Regulatory Counsel before any notice is filed.
Attach the supporting evidence — investigation file, complaint, restitution record — to the termination record.
checklist.done: the termination record carries states, effective date, a state-code classification and the supporting evidence, with for-cause routed to Compliance and Counsel.

checklist.step: File the termination notice to each state within 30 days
actions: In NIPR Gateway open the termination transaction, select the company and state, enter the NPN, the termination effective date and the state's reason code.
Submit within 30 days of the effective date and capture the confirmation number and date.
For a for-cause termination, attach or file the state's required explanatory information with the notice, using the wording Regulatory Counsel approved.
Confirm the termination appears on the PDB appointment history and record the confirmation on the register.
checklist.done: every termination is notified to each affected state within 30 days with a captured confirmation and a PDB status change.

checklist.step: Send the producer notice within 15 days of the state notice
actions: Generate the producer notice from the approved template, restating the same reason given to the state — a mismatch between the two is itself a regulatory problem.
Send it to the producer's address of record within 15 days of the state notice by a method that proves delivery, and retain the delivery evidence.
For a for-cause termination, include the information the state requires the producer to receive and record the send date against the 15-day clock.
File the notice and the delivery proof on the termination record.
checklist.done: the producer notice matches the state reason, is sent within 15 days of the state notice, and delivery is evidenced on the record.

checklist.step: Meet the supplemental-information duty after the notice
actions: Where facts material to the termination reason become known after the state notice, prepare the supplemental report and file it within the state's 30-day window from the date the information became known.
Have Regulatory Counsel review every supplemental report before filing, since the statutory immunity depends on the report being made in the manner the statute prescribes.
Record the date the information became known, the filing date and the day count on the termination record.
Respond to any state request for further information inside the deadline the state states in its request.
checklist.done: every post-notice material fact is reported within 30 days of becoming known, counsel-reviewed, with the day count recorded.

checklist.step: Close down system access and commissions on termination
actions: Disable the producer's agent portal access and quoting rights on the termination effective date, per entity and state.
Set the sell flag to no-sell so no further applications can be submitted under the NPN.
Instruct the Commission Analyst on the treatment of renewal and trail commissions per the contract and any state vesting rule, and suspend payments pending that determination.
Confirm in-flight applications are reassigned to an appointed producer or withdrawn, and notify the affected policyholders' servicing team.
checklist.done: portal access, sell rights and commissions are closed on the effective date and in-flight business is reassigned or withdrawn.

checklist.step: Reconcile the appointment register to the states' records
actions: Each month run the NIPR appointment reconciliation file per appointing company and state and compare it to the internal appointment register.
Investigate every appointment the state shows that the register does not — usually a termination never filed — and every appointment the register shows that the state does not.
Correct the register only after establishing which record is right, using the state's record as governing.
Report unreconciled items over 30 days old to the Producer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: the register reconciles monthly to the states' appointment records with every difference investigated and resolved to the state's record.

checklist.step: Report appointment and termination timeliness
actions: Report monthly: appointment triggers, appointments filed on time, late filings with day counts, terminations notified on time, producer notices sent on time and for-cause reports made.
Name the agencies and entities driving late filings, since the delay is usually in contract paperwork reaching Licensing.
Report every expired statutory window separately with the state and the remediation.
Take the report to the Compliance Committee and the Head of Distribution and record the agreed actions.
checklist.done: monthly timeliness metrics, named drivers of lateness and every expired window are reported with agreed actions recorded.

checklist.step: Archive the transaction evidence
actions: Archive per transaction the trigger evidence, the NIPR confirmation, the state confirmation, the producer notice with delivery proof and any for-cause or supplemental report.
Apply retention of 7 years after the producer relationship ends.
Confirm the index supports retrieval by NPN, appointing company, state and transaction date for DOI inquiries.
Link the archived pack to the appointment register row and close the transaction.
checklist.done: every appointment and termination pack is archived, retention-labelled, indexed by NPN and state, and linked to its register row.

testing.step: Build the population of appointment triggers and termination events
actions: Extract every executed producer or agency contract and every first application submitted by a then-unappointed producer in the month, with dates, entity and state.
Extract every termination with an effective date in the month, with entity, state and classification.
Reconcile the trigger count to the appointment tasks created and investigate any trigger with no task — an undetected trigger is the worst failure in this control.
Sign the population as complete and date it.
testing.done: every contract and first-application trigger and every termination is captured and reconciled to the tasks created.

testing.step: Reconcile the internal register to the states' appointment records
actions: Pull the NIPR appointment reconciliation file per appointing company and state as at the period end.
Compare it to the internal appointment register and list appointments the state shows and the register does not, and the reverse.
Investigate every state-side appointment with no matching register row for an unfiled termination, which carries continuing appointment fees and continuing responsibility.
Quantify the number of stale state-side appointments by company and state.
testing.done: the register reconciles to the states' records with every difference listed, investigated and quantified.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of for-cause terminations, 100% of appointments filed after day 10 of their window, and 100% of triggers with no task.
Select 35 further appointment triggers and 20 further terminations at random using a recorded seed, spread across appointing companies and states.
Record the seed, the population sizes and the selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every transaction rejected by a state during the period as a mandatory item.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all for-cause terminations, late-window appointments, missed triggers, rejections and seeded random items.

testing.step: Recompute the 15-day appointment clock from the trigger evidence
actions: Open the underlying trigger evidence for each sampled appointment — the executed contract or the application submission timestamp — rather than the trigger date field on the task.
Recompute days elapsed to the NIPR submission date using the state's day-counting and business-day convention from the matrix.
Compare to the state's allowed window and to the day count the register records; a difference between the two is a metrics-integrity finding as well as a timing one.
List every appointment filed outside its window with the state and the day count.
testing.done: each sampled appointment's clock is recomputed from primary trigger evidence and compared to both the statutory window and the recorded count.

testing.step: Re-perform the appointment filing in NIPR and confirm the state accepted it
actions: Open the PDB appointment section for each sampled producer and confirm the appointment exists for the right appointing company, state, lines and effective date.
Confirm the confirmed effective date is not later than the first application date, since business taken before the effective date is unappointed business.
Check the appointment lines cover the products the producer actually sold in that state.
Capture the PDB appointment record into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled appointment is confirmed on the PDB with an effective date covering the business written and lines matching the products sold.

testing.step: Recompute the 30-day termination and 15-day producer-notice clocks
actions: For each sampled termination, take the effective date from the termination decision record and recompute days to the NIPR termination submission date against the 30-day window.
Recompute days from the state notice date to the producer notice send date against the 15-day window, using the delivery evidence date rather than the letter date.
Confirm the reason given to the producer is the same reason given to the state and flag every mismatch.
List every window missed with the state, the producer and the day count.
testing.done: both termination clocks are recomputed from primary dates, reason consistency is checked, and every missed window is listed.

testing.step: Test the for-cause reports and the supplemental-information duty
actions: Read the investigation file behind each for-cause termination and confirm the state reason code selected matches the conduct evidenced.

Test the reverse case: review terminations classified as without cause whose files describe conduct the state's codes would require to be reported, since under-reporting is the greater regulatory exposure.
Confirm every supplemental report was filed within 30 days of the information becoming known and was counsel-reviewed before filing.
List any unreported reportable conduct as a breach with a self-report recommendation.
testing.done: for-cause classifications are tested in both directions and every supplemental report is proven timely and counsel-reviewed.

testing.step: Test the post-termination system and commission shutdown
actions: For each sampled termination confirm portal access and the sell flag were closed on the effective date, using the system audit log rather than a status field.
Search for applications submitted under the terminated NPN after the effective date and quantify any found.
Trace commission payments made after the effective date and confirm each is supported by a contract or state vesting rule rather than an uncontrolled payment.
List any post-termination submission or unsupported commission as an exception with the amount.
testing.done: access and sell rights are proven closed on the effective date, with any post-termination submission or unsupported commission quantified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the producer NPN, appointing company, state, the window missed, the day count and the business affected.

Assign a root cause — contract reached Licensing late, trigger job missed the first application, state matrix day count wrong, termination never filed, notice sent without delivery proof — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any missed statutory window or unreported for-cause conduct, require Regulatory Counsel's self-report assessment before closure.
Carry every open exception into the next month's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a day count, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a counsel assessment where a statutory window was missed.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the appointment and termination test
actions: Compute on-time rates separately for appointments within 15 days, terminations within 30 days and producer notices within 15 days, against the 100% threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper reference behind each missed window.
Have the independent reviewer, who filed none of the sampled transactions, sign and date the workpaper.

Report the conclusion, the stale state-side appointment count and any unreported for-cause conduct to the Compliance Committee and the Head of Distribution, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with three separate on-time rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date.
